concepts.name: Schedule
concepts.gloss: An ordered sequence of tape procedures applied one after another; the inverse schedule applies the inverses in reverse order.

concepts.name: Iverson bracket
concepts.gloss: The value 1 when a stated condition is true and 0 when it is false.

concepts.name: Axis line
concepts.gloss: The set of entries of a multidimensional array that vary along one chosen axis while all other coordinates stay fixed.

concepts.name: Natural logarithm
concepts.gloss: The logarithm to base e, the base of the natural exponential function, written ln x.

concepts.name: Near-linear time
concepts.gloss: A running time of the form n times a polylogarithmic factor in n, such as n log n or n (log n) squared.

concepts.name: Negacyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: A convolution in which indices that wrap around the sequence length pick up a minus sign.

concepts.name: Neumann series
concepts.gloss: The series of powers of an operator with alternating signs, which inverts I plus a small operator when that operator has norm below one.

concepts.name: Probability
concepts.gloss: A number between 0 and 1 assigned to each event, additive over disjoint events, with 1 for the certain event.

concepts.name: Radix-two factorization
concepts.gloss: The factorization of a Fourier transform of length 2 to the power k into k levels of butterflies.

concepts.name: Real numbers
concepts.gloss: The numbers on the continuous number line, including all integers, fractions and irrational values such as the square root of 2.

concepts.name: Row reduction
concepts.gloss: Elimination of entries by adding multiples of one row to another, which preserves the row space and exposes pivots, the leading nonzero entries of the reduced rows.

concepts.name: Standard basis vector
concepts.gloss: A vector with entry 1 in one fixed coordinate and 0 in every other coordinate.

concepts.name: Symmetric matrix
concepts.gloss: A square matrix equal to its own transpose.

address.name: address string
address.meaning: A binary string of $d$ bits that labels one entry of the array.

address-field.name: field width

address-interchange.name: fixed exponent
address-interchange.meaning: A fixed number below 1, the exponent in the cost bound $O(Vu^{\tau})$.

address-interchange.name: first field block
address-interchange.meaning: The bits of the first of the two address fields, read as a block at matching positions.
address-interchange.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two fields, each read as a block of bits at matching positions; these letters change meaning here.

address-interchange.name: second field block

address-interchange.name: level count
address-interchange.meaning: The number of levels of the recursion, the logarithm to base m of the field width u.

address-interchange.name: smaller calls

address-interchange.name: level index

array-norm.quote: Let $X$ be such an array, and let $u$ range over its entries.

array-norm.name: representative length
array-norm.meaning: The number of coefficients in each representative of an element of the polynomial ring.
array-norm.quote: Here $r$ is the number of coefficients in each representative.

array-norm.name: ring element
array-norm.meaning: An element of the polynomial ring C[y]/(y^r+1), written as a polynomial of degree less than r.
array-norm.quote: Each element $h$ of the ring is written $h = \sum_{\ell=0}^{r-1} h_\ell y^\ell$, where the index $\ell$ runs from $0$ to $r-1$ and $h_\ell$ is the coefficient of $y^\ell$.

array-norm.name: coefficient index
array-norm.meaning: The index of a coefficient of a ring element, running from 0 to r-1.
array-norm.quote: Each element $h$ of the ring is written $h = \sum_{\ell=0}^{r-1} h_\ell y^\ell$, where the index $\ell$ runs from $0$ to $r-1$ and $h_\ell$ is the coefficient of $y^\ell$.

base-two-logarithm.name: base-2 logarithm
base-two-logarithm.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the positive integer $n$ under the paper's convention, which is at least 1.
base-two-logarithm.quote: The base-2 logarithm, written $\lg n$, is a special case of the [Logarithm](logarithm.md) with the base fixed at 2.

base-two-logarithm.name: bound constant
base-two-logarithm.meaning: The fixed constant $2^{-182}$ in the paper's running-time bound.
base-two-logarithm.quote: The constant $\kappa$ is the fixed value $2^{-182}$ in that bound, which says that exact multiplication of two $n$-bit integers takes $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time.

bezout-identity.name: least positive value
bezout-identity.meaning: The least positive value of $\gamma\xi+\rho\zeta$ over all integers $\xi$ and $\zeta$, which equals the greatest common divisor.
bezout-identity.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the least element, and let $\xi'$ and $\zeta'$ be integers with $\Delta=\gamma\xi'+\rho\zeta'$.

bezout-identity.name: trial coefficient
bezout-identity.meaning: The integer that multiplies $\gamma$ in the pair of integers attaining the least positive value $\Delta$.
bezout-identity.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the least element, and let $\xi'$ and $\zeta'$ be integers with $\Delta=\gamma\xi'+\rho\zeta'$.

bezout-identity.name: trial coefficient
bezout-identity.meaning: The integer that multiplies $\rho$ in the pair of integers attaining the least positive value $\Delta$.
bezout-identity.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the least element, and let $\xi'$ and $\zeta'$ be integers with $\Delta=\gamma\xi'+\rho\zeta'$.

bezout-identity.name: quotient
bezout-identity.meaning: The integer quotient when $\gamma$ is divided by $\Delta$.
bezout-identity.quote: Divide $\gamma$ by $\Delta$: write $\gamma=\Theta\Delta+\Gamma$ with integers $\Theta$ and $\Gamma$, where $0\le\Gamma<\Delta$.

bezout-identity.name: remainder
bezout-identity.meaning: The integer remainder when $\gamma$ is divided by $\Delta$, which lies between 0 and $\Delta$ minus one.
bezout-identity.quote: Divide $\gamma$ by $\Delta$: write $\gamma=\Theta\Delta+\Gamma$ with integers $\Theta$ and $\Gamma$, where $0\le\Gamma<\Delta$.

big-omega-notation.name: Big-Omega
big-omega-notation.meaning: The notation $\Omega(h)$ for the set of functions bounded below by a positive constant times $h$ for all large inputs, so that $u(N)=\Omega(h(N))$ says $u$ lies in that set.
big-omega-notation.quote: The notation $\Omega(h)$ denotes the set of functions $u$ for which there are a constant $C_1>0$ and a threshold $N_0$ such that

big-theta-notation.name: bounded function
big-theta-notation.meaning: The function from input sizes to nonnegative reals whose order is compared with that of $h$.
big-theta-notation.quote: Here $f$ is the function being bounded, and $h$ is the comparison function; both map input sizes to nonnegative real numbers.

big-theta-notation.name: comparison function
big-theta-notation.meaning: The function from input sizes to nonnegative reals against which $f$ is compared.
big-theta-notation.quote: Here $f$ is the function being bounded, and $h$ is the comparison function; both map input sizes to nonnegative real numbers.

big-theta-notation.name: lower factor
big-theta-notation.meaning: A positive real constant multiplying $h(n)$ in the lower inequality.
big-theta-notation.quote: Here $c_1$ is the lower factor, a positive real constant, and $c_2$ is the upper factor, a positive real constant.

big-theta-notation.name: upper factor
big-theta-notation.meaning: A positive real constant multiplying $h(n)$ in the upper inequality.
big-theta-notation.quote: Here $c_1$ is the lower factor, a positive real constant, and $c_2$ is the upper factor, a positive real constant.

big-theta-notation.name: threshold
big-theta-notation.meaning: The input size from which both inequalities hold.
big-theta-notation.quote: The threshold $n_0$ is an input size from which both inequalities hold.

big-theta-notation.name: stored bit volume
big-theta-notation.meaning: The number of stored bits, which is of order $n$.
big-theta-notation.quote: Here $V$ is the number of stored bits, which is $\Theta(n)$.

bijection.name: source set
bijection.meaning: The set whose elements a map takes as inputs.
bijection.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

bijection.name: target set
bijection.meaning: The set whose elements a map takes as outputs.
bijection.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

bijection.name: map
bijection.meaning: A map from U to W that sends each element of U to one element of W.
bijection.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

bijection.name: source element
bijection.meaning: An arbitrary element of the source set U.
bijection.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

bijection.name: target element
bijection.meaning: An arbitrary element of the target set W.
bijection.quote: for every $\upsilon\in W$ there is some $\sigma\in U$ with $f(\sigma)=\upsilon$.

bijection.name: inverse map
bijection.meaning: The map from W to U that sends each target to the unique source element that f maps onto it.
bijection.quote: So each $\upsilon\in W$ is hit by exactly one $\sigma\in U$, and the inverse $f^{-1}\colon W\to U$ sends $\upsilon$ to that $\sigma$.

bijection.name: singled-out subset
bijection.meaning: A subset of U, the set of elements singled out by the argument; in the paper's interchange it is the Exceptional set of bad addresses.
bijection.quote: For a subset $G\subseteq U$, the set of elements singled out by the argument, write $G^c=U\setminus G$ for its complement.

bijection.name: address set
bijection.meaning: The set of integer addresses on which the steps of a tape procedure act.
bijection.quote: Its steps act on a set of integer addresses, which the paper calls $P$.

bilinear-form.name: vector space
bilinear-form.meaning: The vector space over the field $F$ on which the bilinear form is defined.
bilinear-form.quote: Let $E$ be a vector space over the field $F$ of scalars.

bilinear-form.name: subspace
bilinear-form.meaning: A subspace of $E$: a subset closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
bilinear-form.quote: A *subspace* $\mathcal S$ of $E$ is a subset closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

bilinear-form.name: orthogonal complement
bilinear-form.meaning: The set of vectors of $E$ orthogonal to every vector of the subspace $\mathcal S$.
bilinear-form.quote: Its *orthogonal complement* $\mathcal S^\perp$ is the set of vectors $x$ in $E$ with $\langle x,y\rangle=0$ for every $y$ in $\mathcal S$.

bilinear-form.name: basis vector
bilinear-form.meaning: The $j$-th vector of a fixed basis $e_1,\dots,e_m$ of $E$.
bilinear-form.quote: Fix a basis $e_1,\dots,e_m$ of $E$, where $m$ is the dimension of $E$ and $e_j$ is the $j$-th basis vector; the letter $e$ here does not name an eigenvector.

bilinear-form.name: form matrix
bilinear-form.meaning: The $m\times m$ matrix of the form in the fixed basis, whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is $\langle e_i,e_j\rangle$.
bilinear-form.quote: Let $\mathcal M$ be the $m\times m$ matrix with entries $\mathcal M_{ij}=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle$.

bilinear-form.name: indicator vector
bilinear-form.meaning: The 0-1 vector with entry 1 at each element of the three-element subset $\sigma$ and 0 elsewhere.
bilinear-form.quote: For a three-element subset $\sigma$ of $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$, its *indicator vector* $\mathbf 1_\sigma$ has entry $1$ at each element of $\sigma$ and $0$ elsewhere.

bilinear-map.name: first argument space
bilinear-map.meaning: The vector space that the first argument of the bilinear map is taken from.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $J_1$ be the space of first arguments, $J_2$ the space of second arguments, and $\Psi$ the output space, all over the field $F$.

bilinear-map.name: second argument space
bilinear-map.meaning: The vector space that the second argument of the bilinear map is taken from.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $J_1$ be the space of first arguments, $J_2$ the space of second arguments, and $\Psi$ the output space, all over the field $F$.

bilinear-map.name: output space
bilinear-map.meaning: The vector space that contains the values of the bilinear map.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $J_1$ be the space of first arguments, $J_2$ the space of second arguments, and $\Psi$ the output space, all over the field $F$.

bilinear-map.name: bilinear map
bilinear-map.meaning: The map that sends each pair of arguments to a vector of the output space.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $\pi\colon J_1\times J_2\to\Psi$ send each pair $(\xi,\zeta)$, with $\xi\in J_1$ and $\zeta\in J_2$, to a vector $\pi(\xi,\zeta)$ in $\Psi$.

bilinear-map.name: first argument
bilinear-map.meaning: A vector of the first argument space $J_1$.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $\pi\colon J_1\times J_2\to\Psi$ send each pair $(\xi,\zeta)$, with $\xi\in J_1$ and $\zeta\in J_2$, to a vector $\pi(\xi,\zeta)$ in $\Psi$.

bilinear-map.name: second argument
bilinear-map.meaning: A vector of the second argument space $J_2$.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $\pi\colon J_1\times J_2\to\Psi$ send each pair $(\xi,\zeta)$, with $\xi\in J_1$ and $\zeta\in J_2$, to a vector $\pi(\xi,\zeta)$ in $\Psi$.

bilinear-map.name: exact pointwise product
bilinear-map.meaning: The exact bilinear map that multiplies two arrays entry by entry, with records multiplied modulo $y^r+1$ and divided by $r$.
bilinear-map.quote: The paper's error analysis works with an exact bilinear map $P$, the pointwise product that multiplies the two entries at each address, with products of records taken modulo $y^r+1$ and divided by $r$.

bilinear-map.name: computed first operand
bilinear-map.meaning: A computed approximation of the first operand $\xi$.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $\xi'$ and $\zeta'$ be computed approximations of $\xi$ and $\zeta$, with all four operands disk arrays.

bilinear-map.name: computed second operand
bilinear-map.meaning: A computed approximation of the second operand $\zeta$.
bilinear-map.quote: Let $\xi'$ and $\zeta'$ be computed approximations of $\xi$ and $\zeta$, with all four operands disk arrays.

binary-change-of-basis.name: selected bit count
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The number of selected address bits, which is the length of the column of their values.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Let $m$ be the number of selected bits and $\varsigma=(\varsigma_1,\dots,\varsigma_m)$ the column of their values, each $\varsigma_i\in\mathbb F_2$.

binary-change-of-basis.name: selected bit values
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The column of the values of the selected bits, each an element of the binary field.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Let $m$ be the number of selected bits and $\varsigma=(\varsigma_1,\dots,\varsigma_m)$ the column of their values, each $\varsigma_i\in\mathbb F_2$.

binary-change-of-basis.name: change matrix
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The invertible $m\times m$ matrix over the binary field that specifies the change of basis.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: A binary change of basis is specified by an invertible $m\times m$ matrix $M$ over $\mathbb F_2$, as defined in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).

binary-change-of-basis.name: residual basis vector
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The $j$th vector of the residual basis of directions of an edge, a vector of $\mathbb F_2^m$.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Extend the $\mathbf w_j$ to a basis of $\mathbb F_2^m$ and take these vectors as the first $\varrho$ columns of $M$, so that $M\zeta_j=\mathbf w_j$ for $j\le\varrho$.

binary-change-of-basis.name: residual dimension
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The number of vectors in the residual basis of directions, which counts the basis vectors.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: A residual basis of directions is a basis $\mathbf w_1,\dots,\mathbf w_\varrho$ of an edge's residual, a subspace of $\mathbb F_2^m$, where $\varrho$ is the number of its vectors.

binary-change-of-basis.name: unit vector
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The vector with 1 in position $j$ and 0 elsewhere.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Let $\zeta_j$ be the vector with 1 in position $j$ and 0 elsewhere.

binary-change-of-basis.name: address permutation
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The permutation of addresses that moves the value at each address $\alpha$ to $M\alpha$.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Let $P_M$ be the address permutation that moves the value at each address $\alpha$ to $M\alpha$, so $(P_Mf)(\alpha)=f(M^{-1}\alpha)$ for a function $f$ from addresses to values.

binary-change-of-basis.name: address function
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: A function from addresses to values, which $P_M$ rearranges.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Let $P_M$ be the address permutation that moves the value at each address $\alpha$ to $M\alpha$, so $(P_Mf)(\alpha)=f(M^{-1}\alpha)$ for a function $f$ from addresses to values.

binary-change-of-basis.name: shift
binary-change-of-basis.meaning: The map that shifts each address by the vector $\mathbf u$, so $(X_{\mathbf u}f)(\alpha)=f(\alpha+\mathbf u)$.
binary-change-of-basis.quote: Write $(X_{\mathbf u}f)(\alpha)=f(\alpha+\mathbf u)$ for the shift by $\mathbf u$.

binary-field.name: exclusive or
binary-field.meaning: The addition of the binary field, which gives 1 exactly when its two bits differ.
binary-field.quote: Its addition is exclusive or ($\oplus$), which gives $1$ exactly when its two bits differ

binary-field.name: three-element subset
binary-field.meaning: A three-element subset of the ground set, one of the two subsets compared for being neighbours.
binary-field.quote: In the bit construction, two three-element subsets $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ of the ground set are neighbours when they share exactly one element.

binary-field.name: three-element subset
binary-field.meaning: A three-element subset of the ground set, the second of the two subsets compared for being neighbours.
binary-field.quote: In the bit construction, two three-element subsets $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ of the ground set are neighbours when they share exactly one element.

bit-construction.name: ground set size
bit-construction.meaning: The number of elements in the ground set $[h]$, which is 100 here.
bit-construction.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

bit-construction.name: set of triples
bit-construction.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of the ground set $[h]$.
bit-construction.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

bit-construction.name: triple
bit-construction.meaning: A member of $\mathcal K$, that is, a three-element subset of $[h]$.
bit-construction.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

bit-construction.name: triple
bit-construction.meaning: A member of $\mathcal K$, that is, a three-element subset of $[h]$.
bit-construction.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

bit-construction.name: indicator vector
bit-construction.meaning: The 0-1 vector of length $h$ whose entries are 1 exactly at the elements of the triple $T$.
bit-construction.quote: For $T\in\mathcal K$, let $t_T$ be the $0$-$1$ vector of length $h$ that is $1$ exactly at the elements of $T$.

bit-construction.name: neighbour count
bit-construction.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple $T$, which is the number of triples meeting $T$ in exactly one element.
bit-construction.quote: For a fixed triple $T$, let $z_b$ be the number of triples meeting $T$ in exactly one element, which are the neighbours of $T$.

bit-construction.name: source bank
bit-construction.meaning: The bank of scalars with one entry $\xi_T$ per triple, which the invocation reads.
bit-construction.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

bit-construction.name: target bank
bit-construction.meaning: The bank of scalars with one entry $\eta_S$ per triple, which the invocation updates.
bit-construction.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

bit-construction.name: source entry
bit-construction.meaning: The scalar entry of the source bank $X$ indexed by the triple $T$.
bit-construction.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

bit-construction.name: target entry
bit-construction.meaning: The scalar entry of the target bank $Y$ indexed by the triple $S$.
bit-construction.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

bit-construction.name: side wire
bit-construction.meaning: The scratch wire carrying one scalar for each neighbour pair $(S,T)$.
bit-construction.quote: The invocation also has scratch wires: a side wire $W_{ST}$ for each neighbour pair $(S,T)$, and a central wire $C_\ell$ for each $\ell\in[h]$.

bit-construction.name: central wire
bit-construction.meaning: The scratch wire carrying one scalar for each ground element $\ell$.
bit-construction.quote: The invocation also has scratch wires: a side wire $W_{ST}$ for each neighbour pair $(S,T)$, and a central wire $C_\ell$ for each $\ell\in[h]$.

bit-construction.name: binomial coefficient
bit-construction.meaning: The number of $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set.
bit-construction.quote: The binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ counts the $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set.

bit-network.name: triple
bit-network.meaning: An element of $\mathcal T$, that is, a three-element subset of $[h]$ that indexes a bit of each bank.
bit-network.quote: let $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$ denote elements of $\mathcal T$, which we call triples.

bit-network.name: source bank
bit-network.meaning: The family of bits that a forward invocation reads, with one bit $\Xi_\Delta$ for each triple $\Delta$.
bit-network.quote: The source bank $\Xi$ holds one bit $\Xi_\Delta$ for each triple $\Delta$

bit-network.name: target bank
bit-network.meaning: The family of bits that a forward invocation updates, with one bit $Y_\Delta$ for each triple $\Delta$.
bit-network.quote: the target bank $Y$ holds one bit $Y_\Delta$ for each triple $\Delta$.

bit-network.name: ground element
bit-network.meaning: An element of the ground set $[h]$, which indexes one central wire.
bit-network.quote: For each element $\upsilon$ of $[h]$ there is a central wire $J_\upsilon$.

bit-network.name: central wire
bit-network.meaning: The scratch wire attached to the ground element $\upsilon$.
bit-network.quote: For each element $\upsilon$ of $[h]$ there is a central wire $J_\upsilon$.

bit-network.name: side wire
bit-network.meaning: The scratch wire attached to the ordered neighbouring pair of triples $(\Delta,\Delta')$.
bit-network.quote: For each ordered neighbouring pair $(\Delta,\Delta')$ there is a side wire $\zeta_{\Delta\Delta'}$.

bit-procedure.name: edge matrix
bit-procedure.meaning: The matrix attached to edge e, the difference of the matrices at its endpoints.
bit-procedure.quote: Each edge $e$ has a matrix $A_e$, the difference of its endpoint matrices.

bit-procedure.name: exclusive or
bit-procedure.meaning: Addition over the binary field, applied bit by bit.
bit-procedure.quote: Over the binary field, addition is exclusive or ($\oplus$), taken bit by bit.

bit-procedure.name: capped log exponent
bit-procedure.meaning: The capped logarithm max(0, log_m(s/W)) of s/W, which is below tau.
bit-procedure.quote: Let $\theta=\max(0,\log_m(s/W))$ be the capped logarithm of $s/W$, which is below $\tau$.

bit-reversed-order.name: address bit
bit-reversed-order.meaning: The bit of an address with weight $2^s$, which is 0 or 1.
bit-reversed-order.quote: Write an address as a string of bits $\alpha_{d-1}\cdots\alpha_0$, where $\alpha_s \in \{0,1\}$ is the bit with weight $2^s$, so its position number is $\sum_{s=0}^{d-1}\alpha_s 2^s$.

bit-reversed-order.name: bit-reversal map
bit-reversed-order.meaning: The map on $d$-bit addresses that reverses the order of their bits, whose value is the slot number of an address.
bit-reversed-order.quote: The reversal map $\rho_d$ sends each $d$-bit address to the address with the same bits in the opposite order, $\rho_d(\alpha_{d-1}\cdots\alpha_0)=\alpha_0\cdots\alpha_{d-1}$.

bluestein-chirp-identity.name: chirp position
bluestein-chirp-identity.meaning: An integer position at which the chirp is evaluated, which may be negative or at least $q$.
bluestein-chirp-identity.quote: Let $\sigma$ be an integer position, which may be negative or at least $q$.

bluestein-chirp-identity.name: scaled input
bluestein-chirp-identity.meaning: The vector $u$ with each coordinate divided by its chirp entry.

bluestein-chirp-identity.name: cyclic convolution
bluestein-chirp-identity.meaning: The cyclic convolution of two length-$q$ sequences, with indices taken modulo $q$.
bluestein-chirp-identity.quote: For length-$q$ sequences, $a\ast b$ denotes the cyclic convolution with $(a\ast b)_\ell=\sum_{s=0}^{q-1}a_s\,b_{(\ell-s)\bmod q}$.

bluestein-chirp-identity.name: coordinatewise product
bluestein-chirp-identity.meaning: The product of two vectors taken entry by entry.
bluestein-chirp-identity.quote: Writing $a\cdot b$ for the coordinatewise product, $(a\cdot b)_s=a_sb_s$, this is $\hat u=\frac1\chi\cdot u$.

butterfly.name: butterfly map
butterfly.meaning: The two-point map sending a pair (u, v) to ((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2), applied coefficientwise to records.
butterfly.quote: The butterfly is the two-point map $H_0$ that replaces a pair of values by their half-sum and half-difference.

butterfly.name: first input value
butterfly.meaning: The first of the two input values that a butterfly combines.
butterfly.quote: Let $u$ be the first input value and $v$ the second, and here these letters do not keep the meanings they have on earlier pages.

butterfly.name: second input value
butterfly.meaning: The second of the two input values that a butterfly combines.
butterfly.quote: Let $u$ be the first input value and $v$ the second, and here these letters do not keep the meanings they have on earlier pages.

butterfly.name: bit index
butterfly.meaning: The index of the bit a level acts on, counted from 0 at the least significant end.
butterfly.quote: Let $\Xi$ be the index of the bit a level acts on, counted from $0$ at the least significant end.

carry-propagation.name: position index
carry-propagation.meaning: The position of a coefficient in the list, counted from 0 at the least significant end.
carry-propagation.quote: Here $m$ is the position index: it counts the positions of the list from $0$ at the least significant end.

carry-propagation.name: radix
carry-propagation.meaning: The number $2^b$ of values a digit can take.
carry-propagation.quote: The radix is $Q_0 = 2^b$, the number of values a digit can take, so each digit is a $b$-bit block.

carry-propagation.name: output digit
carry-propagation.meaning: The digit of the binary output at position $m$, an integer from 0 to $Q_0-1$.
carry-propagation.quote: Let $\sigma_m$ be the output digit at position $m$, which lies in $\{0, \dots, Q_0-1\}$.

carry-propagation.name: carry
carry-propagation.meaning: The amount carried into position $m$ from the lower positions.
carry-propagation.quote: Let $\gamma_m$ be the carry into position $m$, the amount carried from the lower positions.

carry-propagation.name: summation index
carry-propagation.meaning: The index running over the positions below $m$ in the sums of the invariant.
carry-propagation.quote: Here $h$ is the summation index, running over the positions below $m$.

ceiling-function.name: real number
ceiling-function.meaning: The real number that the ceiling rounds up to an integer.

ceiling-function.name: integer
ceiling-function.meaning: Any integer, which is its own ceiling.
ceiling-function.quote: The symbol $j$ stands for any integer, and an integer is its own ceiling: $\lceil j \rceil = j$.

chinese-remainder-map.name: axis coordinate
chinese-remainder-map.meaning: The coordinate of position $k$ on axis $\kappa$, an integer from $0$ to $n_\kappa-1$.
chinese-remainder-map.quote: Let $\gamma_\kappa$ be the coordinate of position $k$ on axis $\kappa$, the exponent $\mu_\kappa k$ reduced modulo $n_\kappa$

chinese-remainder-map.name: mixed-radix digit
chinese-remainder-map.meaning: The digit of position $k$ at place $\kappa$, an integer from $0$ to $n_\kappa-1$.
chinese-remainder-map.quote: so the digit of $k$ at place $\kappa$ is written $k_\kappa$, an integer from $0$ to $n_\kappa-1$, and the expansion is

chinese-remainder-map.name: place value
chinese-remainder-map.meaning: The number of distinct digit strings on the axes before axis $\kappa$, namely $n_1\cdots n_{\kappa-1}$.
chinese-remainder-map.quote: The place value of axis $\kappa$ is $\pi_\kappa=n_1\cdots n_{\kappa-1}$, the number of distinct digit strings on the axes before $\kappa$, with $\pi_1=1$.

chinese-remainder-map.name: monomial exponent
chinese-remainder-map.meaning: The exponent of $\nu_\kappa$ in a monomial of the standard basis, an integer from $0$ to $n_\kappa-1$.
chinese-remainder-map.quote: where $\eta_\kappa$, an integer from $0$ to $n_\kappa-1$, is the exponent of $\nu_\kappa$.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: congruence count
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The number of congruences in the system.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: Let $\Xi$ be the number of congruences in the system.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: congruence index
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: Labels one congruence of the system, running from 1 to $\Xi$.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: modulus
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The positive integer modulus of the congruence labelled $\mathcal{L}$.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: For each $\mathcal{L}$, let $M_\mathcal{L}$ be the modulus, a positive integer, and $\varrho_\mathcal{L}$ the residue, an integer.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: residue
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The integer residue of the congruence labelled $\mathcal{L}$.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: For each $\mathcal{L}$, let $M_\mathcal{L}$ be the modulus, a positive integer, and $\varrho_\mathcal{L}$ the residue, an integer.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: unknown integer
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The integer unknown whose residues the congruences prescribe.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: The unknown is an integer $\mathcal{Y}$, and $\mathcal{Y}'$ denotes a second integer to be compared with it.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: product of moduli
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The product of all the moduli, a positive integer.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: Let $\mathcal{N}=M_1M_2\cdots M_\Xi$ be the product of all the moduli, a positive integer.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: second integer
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: A second integer, compared with the unknown $\mathcal{Y}$.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: The unknown is an integer $\mathcal{Y}$, and $\mathcal{Y}'$ denotes a second integer to be compared with it.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: difference of solutions
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The difference of two solutions, which every modulus divides.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: Let $\mathcal{Y}$ and $\mathcal{Y}'$ be solutions, and put $\mathcal{E}=\mathcal{Y}'-\mathcal{Y}$.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: integer cofactor
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The integer by which $M_1\cdots M_\mathcal{L}$ is multiplied to give $\mathcal{E}$ in the induction.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: Suppose $\mathcal{E}=M_1\cdots M_\mathcal{L}\,\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is an integer cofactor.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: inverse coefficient
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The Bézout coefficient of $\mathcal{N}/M_\mathcal{L}$, which is an inverse of $\mathcal{N}/M_\mathcal{L}$ modulo $M_\mathcal{L}$.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: Since they are coprime, [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) gives integers $\varpi_\mathcal{L}$ and $\varsigma_\mathcal{L}$ with $\varpi_\mathcal{L}\,\mathcal{N}/M_\mathcal{L}+\varsigma_\mathcal{L}\,M_\mathcal{L}=1$.

chinese-remainder-theorem.name: cofactor of modulus
chinese-remainder-theorem.meaning: The Bézout coefficient of $M_\mathcal{L}$ in the identity for $\mathcal{N}/M_\mathcal{L}$.
chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: Since they are coprime, [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) gives integers $\varpi_\mathcal{L}$ and $\varsigma_\mathcal{L}$ with $\varpi_\mathcal{L}\,\mathcal{N}/M_\mathcal{L}+\varsigma_\mathcal{L}\,M_\mathcal{L}=1$.

complex-construction.name: triple indicator vector
complex-construction.meaning: The indicator vector of the triple S, the 0-1 vector with a one in each position of S.
complex-construction.quote: The complex construction reads its overlaps from [Indicator vector](indicator-vector.md)s, since $|S\cap T|=t_S^{\mathsf T}t_T$, where $t_S$ is the indicator vector of $S$.

complex-construction.name: extra central wire
complex-construction.meaning: The extra central wire that gathers the sum of all source values.
complex-construction.quote: Its auxiliary wires are side wires $W_{ST}$, one for each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$, central wires $C_\ell$ for $\ell\in[h]$, and an extra central wire $C_*$.

complex-construction.name: central coefficient
complex-construction.meaning: The central coefficient of x_T in y_S, equal to (|S ∩ T| − 1)/2.
complex-construction.quote: The coefficient $\varpi_{ST}=\tfrac12(|S\cap T|-1)$ is the central coefficient of $x_T$ in $y_S$.

complex-construction.name: total wire count
complex-construction.meaning: The total number of wires in the complex construction.
complex-construction.quote: The total number of wires, $W_c$, is

complex-construction.name: smaller-call count
complex-construction.meaning: The total number of smaller calls, the recursive calls made on the edges.
complex-construction.quote: Let $s_c$ be the total number of smaller calls.

complex-construction.name: bank entry count
complex-construction.meaning: The number of entries in each data bank, v^3.
complex-construction.quote: Each bank has $N=v^3$ entries, one wire each.

complex-construction.name: triple count
complex-construction.meaning: The number of triples, the binomial coefficient of h choose 3.
complex-construction.quote: Let $v=\binom h3$ be the number of triples; the letter $v$ changes meaning here.

complex-construction.name: neighbour count
complex-construction.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
complex-construction.quote: Each has $vz_c$ side wires and $c_c$ central wires, where $z_c$ is the number of neighbours of a fixed triple.

complex-construction.name: central wire count
complex-construction.meaning: The number of central wires in each invocation of the complex construction.
complex-construction.quote: Each has $vz_c$ side wires and $c_c$ central wires, where $z_c$ is the number of neighbours of a fixed triple.

complex-construction.name: label dimension
complex-construction.meaning: The dimension of the label space, h^3.
complex-construction.quote: The letter $m$ changes meaning here: it is the dimension of the label space, $m=h^3$.

complex-construction.name: dimension lost
complex-construction.meaning: The dimension lost on the central-wire edges of the complex construction.
complex-construction.quote: $L_c$ is the dimension lost on central-wire edges.

complex-disk.name: complex numbers
complex-disk.meaning: The set of complex numbers, the plane in which the disks lie.
complex-disk.quote: Let $\mathbb{C}$ be the set of complex numbers.

complex-disk.name: disk center
complex-disk.meaning: The fixed center of the disk, a complex number.
complex-disk.quote: Let $\xi$ be the center of the disk, a complex number

complex-disk.name: disk radius
complex-disk.meaning: The fixed nonnegative real radius, the largest allowed distance from the center.
complex-disk.quote: and $\rho$ the radius, a nonnegative real number.

complex-disk.name: generic point
complex-disk.meaning: A generic point of the plane, a complex number tested for membership in the disk.
complex-disk.quote: Let $\zeta$ be a generic point of the plane.

complex-disk.name: closed disk
complex-disk.meaning: The closed disk of center $\xi$ and radius $\rho$, the set of points within distance $\rho$ of $\xi$.
complex-disk.quote: The closed disk $\mathcal{D}(\xi,\rho)$ is the set of points within distance $\rho$ of $\xi$:

complex-disk.name: Gaussian integers
complex-disk.meaning: The set of complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are both integers.
complex-disk.quote: Let $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ be the Gaussian integers, the complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are both integers.

complex-disk.name: Gaussian integer
complex-disk.meaning: A generic element of the Gaussian integers, whose scaled value $2^{-p}\varepsilon$ is a point of the grid disk.
complex-disk.quote: Let $\varepsilon$ be a generic Gaussian integer.

complex-disk.name: grid disk
complex-disk.meaning: The points of the unit disk whose real and imaginary parts are multiples of $2^{-p}$, for precision $p$.
complex-disk.quote: For a precision $p$, the grid disk $\mathcal{D}_p$ is the set

complex-phase-network.name: support
complex-phase-network.meaning: The set of coordinates at which a binary vector is 1.
complex-phase-network.quote: For a binary vector $z$, $\mathrm{supp}(z)$ is the set of coordinates at which $z$ is $1$, and $\mathrm{wt}(z)=|\mathrm{supp}(z)|$ is its Hamming weight, the number of such coordinates read as an integer.

complex-phase-network.name: Hamming weight
complex-phase-network.meaning: The number of coordinates at which a binary vector is 1, read as an integer.
complex-phase-network.quote: For a binary vector $z$, $\mathrm{supp}(z)$ is the set of coordinates at which $z$ is $1$, and $\mathrm{wt}(z)=|\mathrm{supp}(z)|$ is its Hamming weight, the number of such coordinates read as an integer.

complex-phase-network.name: integer representative
complex-phase-network.meaning: The integer 0 or 1 that represents a field element b of the binary field.
complex-phase-network.quote: For $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ is its integer representative.

complex-phase-network.name: normalized Hadamard matrix
complex-phase-network.meaning: The 2 by 2 matrix whose tensor powers give the frames of the phase network.
complex-phase-network.quote: The complex phase network computes its frames by the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) $H^{\otimes m}$ of $H=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, the normalized Hadamard matrix; here $H$ denotes this matrix, not the address chunk of other pages.

complex-phase-network.name: phase exponent
complex-phase-network.meaning: The phase exponent of an address x under label U, the Hamming weight of its projection modulo 4.
complex-phase-network.quote: The phase exponent of an address $x$ is $q_U(x)=\mathrm{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4$.

complex-phase-network.name: phase frame
complex-phase-network.meaning: The frame of a vertex with label U, an operator on arrays of addresses.
complex-phase-network.quote: The frame at a vertex with label $U$, the operator $C_U$, is

complex-phase-network.name: projection onto W
complex-phase-network.meaning: The projection onto a nondegenerate subspace W along its orthogonal complement.
complex-phase-network.quote: For a nondegenerate subspace $W$, $P_W$ is the projection onto $W$ along $W^\perp$.

complex-phase-network.name: diagonal operator
complex-phase-network.meaning: The operator that multiplies the value at each address x by f(x).
complex-phase-network.quote: For a function $f$ on addresses, $\mathrm{diag}_x(f(x))$ is the diagonal operator that multiplies the value at each address $x$ by $f(x)$.

complex-phase-network.name: tail label
complex-phase-network.meaning: The label at the tail of an edge.
complex-phase-network.quote: Each vertex carries one label $U$, a subspace of $\mathbb F_2^m$ with $U\cap U^\perp=0$, where $U^\perp$ is the orthogonal complement; such a subspace is nondegenerate.

complex-phase-network.name: head label
complex-phase-network.meaning: The label at the head of an edge.
complex-phase-network.quote: An edge runs from a tail label $U$ to a head label $V$, and its frame change is $C_VC_U^{-1}$.

complex-phase-network.name: orthogonal sum
complex-phase-network.meaning: A B means that A and B are orthogonal subspaces meeting only in zero, with A+B their orthogonal sum.
complex-phase-network.quote: Write $A\perp B$ when every vector of $A$ is orthogonal to every vector of $B$ and $A\cap B=0$, so that $A+B$ is their orthogonal sum.

complex-phase-network.name: orthogonal residual
complex-phase-network.meaning: The orthogonal complement of the smaller label of an edge inside the larger one.
complex-phase-network.quote: The orthogonal residual $\Delta$ of an edge is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one.

complex-phase-network.name: orthonormal basis
complex-phase-network.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the orthogonal residual, a set of vectors v with v dot v equal to 1 that are pairwise orthogonal.
complex-phase-network.quote: Let $\mathcal O$ be an orthonormal basis of $\Delta$, a set of vectors $v$ with $v\cdot v=1$ and $v\cdot v'=0$ for distinct $v,v'\in\mathcal O$.

complex-phase-network.name: edge sign
complex-phase-network.meaning: The sign in {1, -1} that matches the weight of basis vector v on an edge, up to sign for the edge direction.
complex-phase-network.quote: Let $\varepsilon_v\in\{1,-1\}$ with $\varepsilon_v\equiv\mathrm{wt}(v)\pmod 4$ on an increasing edge and $\varepsilon_v\equiv-\mathrm{wt}(v)\pmod 4$ on a decreasing edge.

complex-phase-network.name: first kernel coefficient
complex-phase-network.meaning: The complex number (1+i)/2, the diagonal coefficient of a two-point kernel.
complex-phase-network.quote: Set $\tau_0=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $\tau_1=\frac{1-i}{2}$; here $\tau$ names these coefficients, not the exponent of the address-interchange page.

complex-phase-network.name: second kernel coefficient
complex-phase-network.meaning: The complex number (1-i)/2, the off-diagonal coefficient of a two-point kernel.
complex-phase-network.quote: Set $\tau_0=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $\tau_1=\frac{1-i}{2}$; here $\tau$ names these coefficients, not the exponent of the address-interchange page.

complex-phase-network.name: translation by v
complex-phase-network.meaning: The operator sending a function f to (X_v f)(x) = f(x+v) on addresses.
complex-phase-network.quote: For a binary vector $v$ (the letter $v$ names vectors here, not the vertices of other pages), $X_v$ is the translation by $v$ on functions of addresses.

complex-phase-network.name: two-point kernel
complex-phase-network.meaning: The operator tau_0 I + tau_1 X_v, one factor of an edge change.
complex-phase-network.quote: Call $K_v=\tau_0 I+\tau_1 X_v$ the two-point kernel for $v$.

complex-phase-network.name: route label
complex-phase-network.meaning: The label span(e_1, ..., e_delta) on the route from {0} to the full space.
complex-phase-network.quote: For general $m$, take the route $U_0=\{0\}$ and $U_\delta=\mathrm{span}(e_1,\dots,e_\delta)$ for $1\le\delta\le m$, where $e_\delta$ is the standard basis vector with a single $1$ at position $\delta$.

complex-phase-network.name: standard basis vector
complex-phase-network.meaning: The vector with a single 1 at position delta.
complex-phase-network.quote: For general $m$, take the route $U_0=\{0\}$ and $U_\delta=\mathrm{span}(e_1,\dots,e_\delta)$ for $1\le\delta\le m$, where $e_\delta$ is the standard basis vector with a single $1$ at position $\delta$.

congruence-modulo.name: modulus
congruence-modulo.meaning: A fixed positive integer, the modulus of the congruence, written $\mu$ here in place of the paper's $B_0$.
congruence-modulo.quote: Fix a positive integer $\mu$, the modulus.

congruence-modulo.name: first integer
congruence-modulo.meaning: An integer compared with another integer modulo $\mu$.
congruence-modulo.quote: For integers $\varrho$ and $\varsigma$, we write $\varrho \equiv \varsigma \pmod{\mu}$, read "$\varrho$ is congruent to $\varsigma$ modulo $\mu$", when $\mu$ divides $\varrho-\varsigma$, that is, when $\varrho-\varsigma=\vartheta\mu$ for some integer $\vartheta$, the number of copies of $\mu$ in the difference.

congruence-modulo.name: second integer
congruence-modulo.meaning: An integer compared with the first integer modulo $\mu$.
congruence-modulo.quote: For integers $\varrho$ and $\varsigma$, we write $\varrho \equiv \varsigma \pmod{\mu}$, read "$\varrho$ is congruent to $\varsigma$ modulo $\mu$", when $\mu$ divides $\varrho-\varsigma$, that is, when $\varrho-\varsigma=\vartheta\mu$ for some integer $\vartheta$, the number of copies of $\mu$ in the difference.

congruence-modulo.name: multiple count
congruence-modulo.meaning: The integer multiplier of $\mu$ in a difference, which counts the copies of $\mu$ in it.
congruence-modulo.quote: For integers $\varrho$ and $\varsigma$, we write $\varrho \equiv \varsigma \pmod{\mu}$, read "$\varrho$ is congruent to $\varsigma$ modulo $\mu$", when $\mu$ divides $\varrho-\varsigma$, that is, when $\varrho-\varsigma=\vartheta\mu$ for some integer $\vartheta$, the number of copies of $\mu$ in the difference.

congruence-modulo.name: third integer
congruence-modulo.meaning: A third integer used to check transitivity of congruence.
congruence-modulo.quote: If $\varrho \equiv \varsigma$ and $\varsigma \equiv \varkappa$ for a third integer $\varkappa$, then $\varrho-\varkappa=(\varrho-\varsigma)+(\varsigma-\varkappa)$ is a sum of two multiples of $\mu$, so it is transitive.

congruence-modulo.name: class member
congruence-modulo.meaning: An integer in the residue class of $\varrho$.
congruence-modulo.quote: The class of $\varrho$ is the set of integers $\varpi$ with $\varpi \equiv \varrho \pmod{\mu}$; the classes partition the integers, so each integer lies in exactly one class.

congruence-modulo.name: remainder
congruence-modulo.meaning: The function sending $\varrho$ to its remainder, the unique integer in $\{0,\dots,\mu-1\}$ congruent to $\varrho$.

congruence-modulo.name: second congruent integer
congruence-modulo.quote: Let $\varrho' \equiv \varrho$ and $\varsigma' \equiv \varsigma$ modulo $\mu$, where $\varrho'$ and $\varsigma'$ are integers, with $\varrho'-\varrho=\vartheta\mu$ and $\varsigma'-\varsigma=\vartheta'\mu$, where $\vartheta'$ is the number of copies of $\mu$ in $\varsigma'-\varsigma$.

congruence-modulo.name: second congruent integer
congruence-modulo.quote: Let $\varrho' \equiv \varrho$ and $\varsigma' \equiv \varsigma$ modulo $\mu$, where $\varrho'$ and $\varsigma'$ are integers, with $\varrho'-\varrho=\vartheta\mu$ and $\varsigma'-\varsigma=\vartheta'\mu$, where $\vartheta'$ is the number of copies of $\mu$ in $\varsigma'-\varsigma$.

congruence-modulo.name: second multiple count
congruence-modulo.meaning: The integer multiplier of $\mu$ in the difference $\varsigma'-\varsigma$, which counts the copies of $\mu$ in it.
congruence-modulo.quote: Let $\varrho' \equiv \varrho$ and $\varsigma' \equiv \varsigma$ modulo $\mu$, where $\varrho'$ and $\varsigma'$ are integers, with $\varrho'-\varrho=\vartheta\mu$ and $\varsigma'-\varsigma=\vartheta'\mu$, where $\vartheta'$ is the number of copies of $\mu$ in $\varsigma'-\varsigma$.

congruence-modulo.name: input coefficient
congruence-modulo.meaning: The input coefficient at position $j$ of the carry step.
congruence-modulo.quote: Let $u_j$ be the input coefficient at position $j$ and $\gamma_j$ the carry into position $j$; here $\gamma_j$ is not the scalar of the linear algebra page.

congruence-modulo.name: carry
congruence-modulo.meaning: The carry into position $j$ in the carry step.
congruence-modulo.quote: Let $u_j$ be the input coefficient at position $j$ and $\gamma_j$ the carry into position $j$; here $\gamma_j$ is not the scalar of the linear algebra page.

congruence-modulo.name: output digit
congruence-modulo.meaning: The output digit at position $j$, which is the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $\mu$.
congruence-modulo.quote: Here $c_j$ is the output digit at position $j$, the paper's $d_j$, and $\mu$ is the paper's $B_0$.

convolution.name: entries per input
convolution.meaning: The number of entries in each of the two input sequences.
convolution.quote: Let $u$ and $v$ be two input sequences, and let $L$ be the number of entries in each, so $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{L-1})$ and $v=(v_0,\dots,v_{L-1})$.

convolution.name: first input
convolution.meaning: The first input sequence, of $L$ entries.
convolution.quote: Let $u$ and $v$ be two input sequences, and let $L$ be the number of entries in each, so $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{L-1})$ and $v=(v_0,\dots,v_{L-1})$.

convolution.name: second input
convolution.meaning: The second input sequence, of $L$ entries.
convolution.quote: Let $u$ and $v$ be two input sequences, and let $L$ be the number of entries in each, so $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{L-1})$ and $v=(v_0,\dots,v_{L-1})$.

convolution.name: position in u
convolution.meaning: A position of an entry of $u$, from 0 to $L-1$.
convolution.quote: Here $i$ and $h$ are positions in $u$ and $v$, and $p$ is the position of an output entry.

convolution.name: position in v
convolution.meaning: A position of an entry of $v$, from 0 to $L-1$.
convolution.quote: Here $i$ and $h$ are positions in $u$ and $v$, and $p$ is the position of an output entry.

convolution.name: output position
convolution.meaning: The position of an entry of the convolution $w$, from 0 to $2L-2$.
convolution.quote: Here $i$ and $h$ are positions in $u$ and $v$, and $p$ is the position of an output entry.

convolution.name: convolution
convolution.meaning: The convolution of $u$ and $v$, a sequence of $2L-1$ entries.
convolution.quote: The convolution $w=u*v$ has $2L-1$ entries, $w_0$ through $w_{2L-2}$, and its $p$-th entry is given by the formula below.

coprime.name: first integer
coprime.meaning: An integer, not both zero, that is the first argument of the gcd.
coprime.quote: Here $\gamma$ and $\rho$ are integers; the letters change meaning from their scalar and exponent uses on other pages.

coprime.name: second integer
coprime.meaning: An integer, not both zero, that is the second argument of the gcd.
coprime.quote: Here $\gamma$ and $\rho$ are integers; the letters change meaning from their scalar and exponent uses on other pages.

coprime.name: family member
coprime.quote: For a family $f_1,\dots,f_J$ of integers, $J$ is the number of members and $f_\sigma$ is the $\sigma$-th member, with $\sigma$ running over $1,\dots,J$ (the letters $f$ and $\sigma$ change meaning here).

coprime.name: family size
coprime.meaning: The number of members of the family, the count of integers in it.
coprime.quote: For a family $f_1,\dots,f_J$ of integers, $J$ is the number of members and $f_\sigma$ is the $\sigma$-th member, with $\sigma$ running over $1,\dots,J$ (the letters $f$ and $\sigma$ change meaning here).

coprime.name: member index
coprime.meaning: An index running over $1,\dots,J$ that numbers the members of the family.
coprime.quote: For a family $f_1,\dots,f_J$ of integers, $J$ is the number of members and $f_\sigma$ is the $\sigma$-th member, with $\sigma$ running over $1,\dots,J$ (the letters $f$ and $\sigma$ change meaning here).

coprime.name: second member index
coprime.meaning: A second index of a family member, distinct from $\sigma$ in the pairwise condition.
coprime.quote: The family is pairwise coprime when $\gcd(f_\sigma,f_{\sigma'})=1$ for all distinct indices $\sigma,\sigma'$.

coprime.name: common multiple candidate
coprime.meaning: An integer that is tested for divisibility by the product of the integers it is divided by.
coprime.quote: Two facts follow. First, if $\gamma$ and $\rho$ both divide an integer $Y$ and $\gcd(\gamma,\rho)=1$, then $\gamma\rho$ divides $Y$.

coprime.name: further integer
coprime.meaning: A further integer, coprime to $\rho$ in the same way that $\gamma$ is.
coprime.quote: Second, if $\gcd(\gamma,\rho)=\gcd(\gamma',\rho)=1$ for a further integer $\gamma'$, then $\gcd(\gamma\gamma',\rho)=1$.

coprime.name: Bézout coefficient
coprime.meaning: An integer with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, one of the Bézout coefficients of $\gamma$ and $\rho$.
coprime.quote: [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) gives integers $\Xi,\Psi$ (Bézout coefficients) with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, so $Y=\gamma(Y\Xi)+\rho(Y\Psi)$.

coprime.name: second Bézout coefficient
coprime.meaning: An integer with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, the coefficient of $\rho$ in that identity.
coprime.quote: [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) gives integers $\Xi,\Psi$ (Bézout coefficients) with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, so $Y=\gamma(Y\Xi)+\rho(Y\Psi)$.

coprime.name: coefficient for further integer
coprime.meaning: An integer with $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$, the coefficient of $\gamma'$ in that identity.
coprime.quote: With $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$ for integers $\Xi',\Psi'$, multiplying the two identities gives $\gamma\gamma'(\Xi\Xi')+\rho(\cdots)=1$.

coprime.name: coefficient of rho
coprime.meaning: An integer with $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$, the coefficient of $\rho$ in that identity.
coprime.quote: With $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$ for integers $\Xi',\Psi'$, multiplying the two identities gives $\gamma\gamma'(\Xi\Xi')+\rho(\cdots)=1$.

coprime.name: family product
coprime.meaning: The product $f_1\cdots f_J$ of all members of the family.
coprime.quote: Let $\Pi=f_1\cdots f_J$ be the product of the family.

coprime.name: integers modulo f
coprime.meaning: The integers modulo $f$, whose elements are classes of integers that differ by multiples of $f$.
coprime.quote: Let $\mathbb{Z}/f$ be the integers modulo $f$, whose classes hold integers differing by multiples of $f$.

coprime.name: tuple group
coprime.meaning: The group of tuples $(x_1,\dots,x_J)$ with $x_\sigma$ in $\mathbb{Z}/f_\sigma$, under entrywise addition.
coprime.quote: Let $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}/f_1\times\cdots\times\mathbb{Z}/f_J$ be the group of tuples under entrywise addition; it has $\Pi$ elements.

coprime.name: all-ones tuple
coprime.meaning: The tuple $(1,\dots,1)$, with entry 1 in every place.

coprime.name: prefix product
coprime.meaning: The product of the first $\sigma-1$ members of the family, with $\Pi_1=1$.
coprime.quote: The split uses the prefix products $\Pi_\sigma=f_1\cdots f_{\sigma-1}$, with $\Pi_1=1$.

coprime.name: inverse multiplier
coprime.meaning: An integer that is an inverse of $\Pi_\sigma$ modulo $f_\sigma$, equal to the coefficient $\Xi$ of $\Pi_\sigma$.
coprime.quote: Each $\Pi_\sigma$ is coprime to $f_\sigma$, so $\Pi_\sigma\Xi+f_\sigma\Psi=1$ for some integers, and $\Upsilon_\sigma=\Xi$ satisfies $\Pi_\sigma\Upsilon_\sigma\equiv1\pmod{f_\sigma}$.

cost-table.name: bit length
cost-table.meaning: The rounded-up base-2 logarithm of $n$, which counts the bits of $n$.
cost-table.quote: Write $b = \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ for the rounded-up base-2 logarithm of $n$, the number of bits of $n$ (the letter $b$ changes meaning here).

cost-table.name: padded cell count
cost-table.meaning: The number of cells of the padded box, a power of two in $[4n/b, 8n/b)$.
cost-table.quote: Write $T$ for the number of cells of the padded box (the letter $T$ changes meaning here).

cost-table.name: axis count
cost-table.meaning: The number of axes of the padded box.
cost-table.quote: Write $d = \lfloor b^{\epsilon} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ for the number of axes of the box (the letter $d$ changes meaning here), and $K = \lfloor d^{c} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ for the number of bits in each address chunk, a run of consecutive address bits (the letter $K$ changes meaning here).

cost-table.name: chunk width
cost-table.meaning: The number of bits in each address chunk.
cost-table.quote: Write $d = \lfloor b^{\epsilon} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ for the number of axes of the box (the letter $d$ changes meaning here), and $K = \lfloor d^{c} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ for the number of bits in each address chunk, a run of consecutive address bits (the letter $K$ changes meaning here).

cost-table.name: axis exponent
cost-table.meaning: The exponent with $r = 2^{\ell}$, which counts the factors of two in $r$.
cost-table.quote: Write $\ell = \lceil \log_2 T/d \rceil$ for the exponent with $r = 2^{\ell}$ (the letter $\ell$ changes meaning here).

cost-table.name: dimension exponent
cost-table.meaning: A fixed positive exponent, equal to $2^{-75}$.
cost-table.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

cost-table.name: chunk exponent
cost-table.meaning: A fixed positive exponent, equal to $2^{-56}$.
cost-table.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

cost-table.name: exchange exponent
cost-table.meaning: The exponent $1-2^{-50}$ in the cost of a chunk exchange.
cost-table.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

cost-table.name: round exponent
cost-table.meaning: The exponent $1-2^{-54}$ in the cost of a simultaneous round.
cost-table.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

cost-table.name: small exponent
cost-table.meaning: A fixed small exponent, equal to $1/16$.
cost-table.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

cost-table.name: line-map factor
cost-table.meaning: The factor that scales the cost of the line maps.
cost-table.quote: The factor $\alpha$ scales the cost of the line maps, a line being a slice of the box along one axis (the letter $\alpha$ changes meaning here).

cyclic-convolution.name: formal variable
cyclic-convolution.meaning: A formal variable in which the polynomials of this page are written; it is a symbol, not a number.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Identify $a$ with $a(w) = \sum_{s=0}^{n-1} a_s w^s$, where $w$ is a formal variable (a symbol, not a number).

cyclic-convolution.name: multiplier
cyclic-convolution.meaning: A positive integer with a modular inverse modulo $n_\kappa$, one for each axis.
cyclic-convolution.quote: The layout relies on a [Modular inverse](modular-inverse.md) modulo $n_\kappa$ for each multiplier $\mu_\kappa$, which is a positive integer.

cyclic-convolution.name: axis variable
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The variable of axis $\kappa$, whose $n_\kappa$-th power is $1$.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $\nu_\kappa$ be the variable of axis $\kappa$, with $\nu_\kappa^{n_\kappa} = 1$

cyclic-convolution.name: layout map
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The map sending $w$ to the product of the axis variables raised to the powers $\mu_\kappa$.
cyclic-convolution.quote: let $\Phi$ be the map that sends $w$ to $\prod_\kappa \nu_\kappa^{\mu_\kappa}$.

cyclic-convolution.name: axis index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: An index $1 \le \kappa \le D$ numbering the axes; on this page it is not the constant of the time bound.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Here $\kappa$ is an axis index, not the constant $\kappa$ of the time bound, and axis $\kappa$ has length $n_\kappa$, the number of values its coordinate takes.

cyclic-convolution.name: axis length
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The number of values the coordinate of axis $\kappa$ takes.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Here $\kappa$ is an axis index, not the constant $\kappa$ of the time bound, and axis $\kappa$ has length $n_\kappa$, the number of values its coordinate takes.

cyclic-convolution.name: phase sequence
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The phase $e^{-\pi i s^2/q}$ at position $s$, used only in the middle-transform identity.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $\phi_s = e^{-\pi i s^2/q}$ and $\psi_\delta = e^{\pi i \delta^2/q}$ for integers $s$ and $\delta$; here $\phi$ and $\psi$ are local names, used only in this section.

cyclic-convolution.name: phase kernel
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The sequence $e^{\pi i \delta^2/q}$ at offset $\delta$, used only in the middle-transform identity.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $\phi_s = e^{-\pi i s^2/q}$ and $\psi_\delta = e^{\pi i \delta^2/q}$ for integers $s$ and $\delta$; here $\phi$ and $\psi$ are local names, used only in this section.

cyclic-coordinate.name: coordinate index
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: An integer from 1 to d that names one coordinate of the array.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: Let $\sigma$ name one coordinate, running from $1$ to $d$.

cyclic-coordinate.name: cyclic length
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: The number of positions along coordinate sigma before its indices wrap around.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: Let $n_\sigma$ be the cyclic length of coordinate $\sigma$, the number of positions along that axis before indices wrap around.

cyclic-coordinate.name: shortened-coordinate count
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: The number of coordinates whose length is r/2 in the padded box.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: Let $\varkappa$ be the number of coordinates of length $r/2$.

cyclic-coordinate.name: box size
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: The number of entries of the padded box, a power of two; on this page only, not the three-element subsets of other pages.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: The box holds $T$ entries, the box size, a power of two ($T$ here, not the three-element subsets of other pages).

cyclic-coordinate.name: twist position
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: An integer position from 0 to r-1 on the last coordinate, at which the phase twist acts.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: Let $\upsilon$ be a position on the last axis, an integer from $0$ to $r-1$.

cyclic-coordinate.name: second position
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: A second position on the last coordinate, paired with upsilon in a sum.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: Let $\upsilon'$ be a second such position.

cyclic-coordinate.name: reduced position
cyclic-coordinate.meaning: The position in the range from 0 to r-1 that equals the sum of upsilon and upsilon' minus r when the sum wraps.
cyclic-coordinate.quote: If $\upsilon+\upsilon'\ge r$, let $\upsilon''$ be the reduced position, so $\upsilon+\upsilon'=\upsilon''+r$ with $0\le\upsilon''<r$.

cyclic-group.name: generator
cyclic-group.meaning: The fixed element whose powers make up the cyclic group.
cyclic-group.quote: Let $\upsilon$ be a fixed element of a group, its *generator*.

cyclic-group.name: exponent
cyclic-group.meaning: An integer exponent of $\upsilon$ in the power $\upsilon^\vartheta$.
cyclic-group.quote: For an integer $\vartheta$, $\upsilon^\vartheta$ is the product of $\vartheta$ copies of $\upsilon$, with $\upsilon^{-1}$ the inverse of $\upsilon$ and $\upsilon^0=1$.

cyclic-group.name: order of an element
cyclic-group.meaning: The number of distinct powers of an element, equal to the least positive integer whose power is 1.
cyclic-group.quote: The *order* of $\upsilon$ is the least positive integer $\vartheta$ with $\upsilon^\vartheta=1$, written $\operatorname{ord}(\upsilon)$, the number of distinct powers of $\upsilon$ when that is finite.

cyclic-group.name: Chinese-remainder map
cyclic-group.meaning: The map from the cyclic group generated by $\upsilon$ to $G$ that sends $\upsilon^\vartheta$ to $\vartheta\mu$.
cyclic-group.quote: Let $\Gamma$ send $\upsilon$ to $\mu$ and $\upsilon^\vartheta$ to $\vartheta\mu$, the tuple whose $\sigma$-th entry is $\vartheta\mu_\sigma$ mod $f_\sigma$.

cyclic-shift.name: block length
cyclic-shift.meaning: The number of positions in the block that the shift rotates, a count of those positions.
cyclic-shift.quote: Let $J$ be the number of positions in the block.

cyclic-shift.name: position
cyclic-shift.meaning: A position in the block, numbered from 0 to J-1.
cyclic-shift.quote: Let $\zeta$ be a position, numbered $0$ to $J-1$, and let $\xi_\zeta$ be the value stored there.

cyclic-shift.name: stored value
cyclic-shift.meaning: The value stored at position zeta of the block.
cyclic-shift.quote: Let $\zeta$ be a position, numbered $0$ to $J-1$, and let $\xi_\zeta$ be the value stored there.

cyclic-shift.name: offset
cyclic-shift.meaning: The amount of rotation, an integer taken modulo J.
cyclic-shift.quote: Let $\upsilon$ be the offset, an integer taken modulo $J$.

cyclic-shift.name: stored bit volume
cyclic-shift.meaning: The number of stored bits in the array, a count of its data bits.
cyclic-shift.quote: Let $V$ be the number of stored bits.

destination-rank.name: address
destination-rank.meaning: The address of a record, given by its three chunk values $\Psi_1$, $\Psi_2$, $\Psi_3$.
destination-rank.quote: It is stored at an address $\Psi=(\Psi_1,\Psi_2,\Psi_3)$ of three chunks, named $1$, $2$ and $3$, where $\Psi_1$, $\Psi_2$, $\Psi_3$ are its chunk values.

destination-rank.name: destination address
destination-rank.meaning: The destination address of the record at $\Psi$, the address to which it moves.
destination-rank.quote: Let $\Psi'$ be the destination of the record at $\Psi$, as defined below.

destination-rank.name: rank
destination-rank.meaning: The position of the record at an address among the records in stream order, counted from 0.
destination-rank.quote: The rank $\operatorname{rank}(\Psi)$ of the record at $\Psi$ is its position among the records in stream order, counted from $0$.

destination-rank.name: chunk stride
destination-rank.meaning: The amount the rank changes when a chunk rises by one with the other two fixed; $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$, $\sigma_3$ are the strides of chunks 1, 2 and 3.
destination-rank.quote: Let $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$, $\sigma_3$ be the strides of the chunks: the stride of a chunk is the amount the rank changes when that chunk rises by one with the other two fixed.

destination-rank.name: exceptional addresses
destination-rank.meaning: The set of addresses whose records the correction moves.
destination-rank.quote: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the set of exceptional addresses (the paper's $B$), where some guard value lies too close to the edge of its range for the packed addition to be exact.

destination-rank.name: correction
destination-rank.meaning: The permutation of addresses by which the correction moves records.

destination-rank.name: ideal permutation
destination-rank.meaning: The permutation of addresses that the packed addition should perform.
destination-rank.quote: Let $T_0$ be the ideal permutation of addresses that the packed addition should perform, and let $S_0$ be the packed approximation, which agrees with $T_0$ off $\mathcal{E}$.

destination-rank.name: packed approximation
destination-rank.meaning: The packed addition that agrees with the ideal permutation $T_0$ off the exceptional addresses.
destination-rank.quote: Let $T_0$ be the ideal permutation of addresses that the packed addition should perform, and let $S_0$ be the packed approximation, which agrees with $T_0$ off $\mathcal{E}$.

destination-rank.name: payload bits
destination-rank.meaning: The number of payload bits in each record.
destination-rank.quote: Each record is a block of $R$ payload bits, where $R$ is the number of payload bits in a record.

destination-rank.name: stream bit count
destination-rank.meaning: The number of bits in the stream, $MR$.
destination-rank.quote: Let $V=MR$ be the number of bits in the stream, so $M\le V$.

diagonal-scaling.name: coordinate label set
diagonal-scaling.meaning: The finite set of coordinate labels, one for each coordinate of the vectors.
diagonal-scaling.quote: Let $\mathcal I$ be the finite set of coordinate labels, one for each coordinate of the vectors.

diagonal-scaling.name: coordinate label
diagonal-scaling.meaning: A label naming one coordinate of the vectors, an element of the set of labels.
diagonal-scaling.quote: Each label $\iota\in\mathcal I$ names one coordinate, and $x_\iota$ is the value of a vector $x$ at that coordinate.

diagonal-scaling.name: array space
diagonal-scaling.meaning: The vector space of arrays indexed by the labels, with entries in F.
diagonal-scaling.quote: Write $F^{\mathcal I}$ for the vector space of arrays $x=(x_\iota)_{\iota\in\mathcal I}$ with entries $x_\iota\in F$.

diagonal-scaling.name: scalar family
diagonal-scaling.meaning: A family of scalars, one for each label, that sets the scaling.
diagonal-scaling.quote: Given a family of scalars $\upsilon=(\upsilon_\iota)_{\iota\in\mathcal I}$ with each $\upsilon_\iota\in F$, the diagonal scaling $\Delta_\upsilon$ is the map

diagonal-scaling.name: diagonal scaling
diagonal-scaling.meaning: The map sending each array to the array whose $\iota$-th entry is $\upsilon_\iota$ times its $\iota$-th entry.
diagonal-scaling.quote: Given a family of scalars $\upsilon=(\upsilon_\iota)_{\iota\in\mathcal I}$ with each $\upsilon_\iota\in F$, the diagonal scaling $\Delta_\upsilon$ is the map

diagonal-scaling.name: second scalar family
diagonal-scaling.meaning: A second family of scalars, one for each label, used to compose two scalings.
diagonal-scaling.quote: Second, for a second family $\upsilon'=(\upsilon'_\iota)_{\iota\in\mathcal I}$ of scalars, $\Delta_\upsilon\Delta_{\upsilon'}=\Delta_{\upsilon\upsilon'}$, where $(\upsilon\upsilon')_\iota=\upsilon_\iota\upsilon'_\iota$.

diagonal-scaling.name: one-bit count
diagonal-scaling.meaning: The number of selected bits of the address $\alpha$ that equal $1$.
diagonal-scaling.quote: For an address $\alpha$, let $\operatorname{ones}(\alpha)$ be the number of selected bits of $\alpha$ equal to $1$.

directed-graph.name: directed graph
directed-graph.meaning: The directed graph, written as the pair of its vertex set V and its edge set E.
directed-graph.quote: A directed graph is a pair $G = (V, E)$ of a set $V$ of vertices and a set $E$ of ordered pairs of vertices.

directed-graph.name: vertex set
directed-graph.meaning: The set of vertices of the directed graph, the points that edges join.
directed-graph.quote: A directed graph is a pair $G = (V, E)$ of a set $V$ of vertices and a set $E$ of ordered pairs of vertices.

directed-graph.name: edge set
directed-graph.meaning: The set of directed edges of the directed graph, each an ordered pair of vertices.
directed-graph.quote: A directed graph is a pair $G = (V, E)$ of a set $V$ of vertices and a set $E$ of ordered pairs of vertices.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: transform length
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The number of coordinates of each vector the transform acts on, a positive integer.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $q$ be the transform length, the number of coordinates of each vector the transform acts on, a positive integer.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: primitive root of unity
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The primitive q-th root of unity $e^{-2\pi\sqrt{-1}/q}$, whose powers below the q-th are not 1.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Write $\omega = e^{-2\pi\sqrt{-1}/q}$ for the primitive $q$-th root of unity.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: integer exponent
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An integer exponent of omega that ranges strictly between 0 and q in the primitivity condition.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Then $\omega^q = 1$, and $\omega^\mu \ne 1$ for each integer exponent $\mu$ with $0 < \mu < q$, so no smaller positive power of $\omega$ equals $1$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input vector
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A vector of q complex numbers, whose coordinates f_s are the inputs of the transform.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $f = (f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{q-1})$ be a vector of $q$ complex numbers, and let $s$ and $\ell$ be integer indices running over $0, 1, \ldots, q-1$, where $s$ labels an input coordinate $f_s$ and $\ell$ labels an output coordinate.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input index
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An integer index running from 0 to q minus 1 that labels an input coordinate f_s.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $f = (f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{q-1})$ be a vector of $q$ complex numbers, and let $s$ and $\ell$ be integer indices running over $0, 1, \ldots, q-1$, where $s$ labels an input coordinate $f_s$ and $\ell$ labels an output coordinate.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: output index
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An integer index running from 0 to q minus 1 that labels an output coordinate of the transform.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $f = (f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{q-1})$ be a vector of $q$ complex numbers, and let $s$ and $\ell$ be integer indices running over $0, 1, \ldots, q-1$, where $s$ labels an input coordinate $f_s$ and $\ell$ labels an output coordinate.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: discrete Fourier transform
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The map of length q that sends a vector f to the vector whose coordinates are the normalized weighted sums of f.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: The discrete Fourier transform of length $q$ is the map $F_q$ sending $f$ to the vector $F_q f$ with coordinates

discrete-fourier-transform.name: opposite transform
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The same map as F_q with the positive sign in the exponent, which undoes F_q up to the factor q.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: $F_q^+$ denotes the same map with the positive sign, $(F_q^+ f)_\ell = \frac{1}{q} \sum_{s=0}^{q-1} f_s\, \omega^{-s\ell}$, which replaces $\omega$ by $\omega^{-1}$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: dummy index
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A second summation index running over 0 to q minus 1, used in the inversion calculation.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: To see that $F_q^+$ undoes $F_q$ up to the factor $q$, take a second dummy index $\sigma$ running over $0, 1, \ldots, q-1$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: index difference
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The integer sigma minus ell, with absolute value less than q.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: linear map on q-vectors
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A generic linear map from q-vectors to q-vectors, tested for being a contraction.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: A linear map $K$ on $q$-vectors is a contraction when $\|Kf\| \le \|f\|$ for every $f$.

dual-space.name: vector space
dual-space.meaning: A vector space over the field F, whose linear functionals form the dual space.
dual-space.quote: Let $U$ be a vector space over the field $F$.

dual-space.name: dual space
dual-space.meaning: The vector space of all linear functionals on U.
dual-space.quote: The dual space $U^*$ collects every [Linear functional](linear-functional.md) on $U$ into one vector space.

dual-space.name: linear functional
dual-space.meaning: A generic element of the dual space U^*, which is a linear map from U to F.
dual-space.quote: The elements of $U^*$ are written $f$; each is a map $f: U \to F$ that is linear, so $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ and $f(cx)=cf(x)$ for vectors $x,y$ and scalars $c$ in $F$.

dual-space.name: example functional
dual-space.meaning: The linear functional on R^2 sending x to 3x_1 - x_2.
dual-space.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the functional $\sigma(x)=3x_1-x_2$ and $\rho$ the functional $\rho(x)=x_1$.

dual-space.name: second example functional
dual-space.meaning: The linear functional on R^2 sending x to x_1.
dual-space.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the functional $\sigma(x)=3x_1-x_2$ and $\rho$ the functional $\rho(x)=x_1$.

eigenvalue.name: vector space
eigenvalue.meaning: The vector space on which the linear operator T acts.
eigenvalue.quote: Here $U$ is a vector space and $T$ a linear operator on $U$.

eigenvalue.name: eigenvalue
eigenvalue.meaning: A scalar for which $Tv=\lambda v$ holds for some nonzero vector $v$ in $U$.
eigenvalue.quote: A scalar $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $T$ when $Tv=\lambda v$ for some nonzero vector $v$ in $U$, and $v$ is then an eigenvector.

eigenvalue.name: eigenvector
eigenvalue.meaning: A nonzero vector $v$ in $U$ with $Tv=\lambda v$ for an eigenvalue $\lambda$, called an eigenvector.
eigenvalue.quote: A scalar $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $T$ when $Tv=\lambda v$ for some nonzero vector $v$ in $U$, and $v$ is then an eigenvector.

eigenvalue.name: coordinate count
eigenvalue.meaning: The number of rational entries in each vector of $\mathbb{Q}^m$, at least 2.
eigenvalue.quote: Here $\mathbb{Q}^m$ is the set of vectors with $m\ge2$ rational entries.

eigenvalue.name: all-ones vector
eigenvalue.meaning: The vector whose entries are all 1.
eigenvalue.quote: Write $\mathbf 1$ for the all-ones vector, so the all-one matrix $J$ is $\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$.

eigenvalue.name: all-one matrix
eigenvalue.meaning: The matrix with every entry 1, equal to $\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$.
eigenvalue.quote: Write $\mathbf 1$ for the all-ones vector, so the all-one matrix $J$ is $\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$.

eigenvalue.name: symmetric form matrix
eigenvalue.meaning: A symmetric matrix whose form $x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ is tested for nondegeneracy.
eigenvalue.quote: Eigenvalues test the nondegeneracy of a [symmetric matrix](symmetric-matrix.md) $A$.

eigenvalue.name: average entry
eigenvalue.meaning: The average entry of $x$, so that the part of $x$ along $\mathbf 1$ is $\gamma\mathbf 1$.
eigenvalue.quote: Every $x\in\mathbb{Q}^m$ splits as $x=\gamma\mathbf 1+x_0$, where $\gamma$ is the average entry of $x$ and $x_0$ has entries summing to zero.

eigenvalue.name: zero-sum part
eigenvalue.meaning: The part of $x$ with entries summing to zero, so that $x=\gamma\mathbf 1+x_0$.
eigenvalue.quote: Every $x\in\mathbb{Q}^m$ splits as $x=\gamma\mathbf 1+x_0$, where $\gamma$ is the average entry of $x$ and $x_0$ has entries summing to zero.

endpoint-operator.name: role endpoint operator
endpoint-operator.meaning: The operator $D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(\ell))}D_{\mathrm{source}(\ell)}^{-1}$ that the frames at the ends of the route of role $\ell$ give to its array.
endpoint-operator.quote: Write $\mathcal{E}_\ell$ for the endpoint operator of role $\ell$, $D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(\ell))}\,D_{\mathrm{source}(\ell)}^{-1}$, with $\mathrm{source}(\ell)$ and $\mathrm{sink}(\rho(\ell))$ the vertices where the two roles start and end.

established-multiplier.name: input bit length
