ring-homomorphism.name: ring
ring-homomorphism.meaning: A ring, the domain of the homomorphism $\mathcal{H}$.

ring-homomorphism.name: ring
ring-homomorphism.meaning: A ring, the codomain of the homomorphism $\mathcal{H}$.

ring-homomorphism.name: ring homomorphism
ring-homomorphism.meaning: A map between rings that preserves sums, products and $1$.
ring-homomorphism.quote: A map $\mathcal{H}:\mathcal{R}\to\mathcal{S}$ is a ring homomorphism when, for all $\xi,\zeta\in\mathcal{R}$,

ring-homomorphism.name: indeterminate
ring-homomorphism.meaning: A formal variable, not a number, of the polynomial rings $\mathcal{Q}_1$ and $\mathcal{Q}_3$.
ring-homomorphism.quote: An indeterminate $\mathcal{X}$ is a formal variable, not a number.

ring-homomorphism.name: quotient ring
ring-homomorphism.meaning: The ring of complex polynomials in $\mathcal{X}$ modulo $\mathcal{X}^2-1$.
ring-homomorphism.quote: Let $\mathcal{Q}_1=\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{X}]/(\mathcal{X}^2-1)$, the quotient ring of complex polynomials in which every multiple of $\mathcal{X}^2-1$ counts as zero.

ring-homomorphism.name: substitute
ring-homomorphism.meaning: An element of a commutative ring with square 1, substituted for $\mathcal{X}$.

ring-homomorphism.name: second indeterminate
ring-homomorphism.meaning: A formal variable, the indeterminate of $\mathcal{Q}_2$.

ring-homomorphism.name: quotient ring
ring-homomorphism.meaning: The ring of complex polynomials in $\mathcal{Y}$ modulo $\mathcal{Y}^2+1$.

ring-homomorphism.name: inverse isomorphism
ring-homomorphism.meaning: The homomorphism $\mathcal{Q}_2\to\mathcal{Q}_1$ that inverts $\mathcal{H}$ in Example 1.

ring-homomorphism.name: cyclic quotient ring
ring-homomorphism.meaning: The ring $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{X}]$ modulo $\mathcal{X}^6-1$, the source of the paper's map.
ring-homomorphism.quote: Let $\mathcal{Q}_3=\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{X}]/(\mathcal{X}^6-1)$, and let $\mathcal{Z}_1$ and $\mathcal{Z}_2$ be the indeterminates of the cyclic axes of lengths 2 and 3, so the target is $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{Z}_1,\mathcal{Z}_2]/(\mathcal{Z}_1^2-1,\mathcal{Z}_2^3-1)$.

ring-homomorphism.name: axis indeterminate
ring-homomorphism.meaning: The indeterminate of the cyclic axis of length 2 in the target ring.
ring-homomorphism.quote: Let $\mathcal{Q}_3=\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{X}]/(\mathcal{X}^6-1)$, and let $\mathcal{Z}_1$ and $\mathcal{Z}_2$ be the indeterminates of the cyclic axes of lengths 2 and 3, so the target is $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{Z}_1,\mathcal{Z}_2]/(\mathcal{Z}_1^2-1,\mathcal{Z}_2^3-1)$.

ring-homomorphism.name: axis indeterminate
ring-homomorphism.meaning: The indeterminate of the cyclic axis of length 3 in the target ring.
ring-homomorphism.quote: Let $\mathcal{Q}_3=\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{X}]/(\mathcal{X}^6-1)$, and let $\mathcal{Z}_1$ and $\mathcal{Z}_2$ be the indeterminates of the cyclic axes of lengths 2 and 3, so the target is $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{Z}_1,\mathcal{Z}_2]/(\mathcal{Z}_1^2-1,\mathcal{Z}_2^3-1)$.

root-of-unity.name: complex number
root-of-unity.meaning: A complex number, which may or may not be a root of unity.

root-of-unity.name: order
root-of-unity.meaning: The number of distinct powers of a root of unity $z$, which equals the least positive integer $q$ with $z^q = 1$.
root-of-unity.quote: For a root of unity $z$, let $q$ denote the order of $z$, the least positive integer with $z^q = 1$; it is also the number of distinct powers $z, z^2, \ldots, z^q$.

root-of-unity.name: polynomial variable
root-of-unity.meaning: The polynomial variable of the quotient ring $\mathbb{C}[y]/(y^4+1)$, which satisfies $y^4 = -1$.
root-of-unity.quote: Here $y$ denotes the polynomial variable of the quotient ring $\mathbb{C}[y]/(y^4+1)$, in which $y^4+1$ is zero, so $y^4 = -1$.

root-of-unity.name: integer exponent
root-of-unity.meaning: An integer exponent, so that $y^a$ is defined for any integer $a$.

running-time-cost.name: input length
running-time-cost.meaning: The number of cells that hold the input, which is the argument of the running time cost.
running-time-cost.quote: The running time cost of a machine is the number of steps it takes on an input, as a worst-case function of $n$, the number of cells that hold the input.

running-time-cost.name: exponent constant
running-time-cost.meaning: The fixed constant $2^{-182}$ in the exponent of the bound $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.
running-time-cost.quote: Here $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ is a fixed constant of the theorem, and its running time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.

running-time-cost.name: machine
running-time-cost.meaning: A machine whose running time cost is being measured.
running-time-cost.quote: For a machine $A$ and an input length $n$, the running time cost is $T_A(n)$, the largest number of steps $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.

running-time-cost.name: running time cost
running-time-cost.meaning: The largest number of steps machine $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.
running-time-cost.quote: For a machine $A$ and an input length $n$, the running time cost is $T_A(n)$, the largest number of steps $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.

running-time-cost.name: example machine
running-time-cost.meaning: The example machine that reads cells from the first cell until it finds a $1$ or reaches the last cell.
running-time-cost.quote: Take the machine $M$ that starts on the first cell.

schedule.name: first procedure
schedule.meaning: The first of three tape procedures in the example schedule, the one applied first.
schedule.quote: Write $\Xi_1$, $\Xi_2$ and $\Xi_3$ for three tape procedures.

schedule.name: second procedure
schedule.meaning: The second of three tape procedures in the example schedule, applied after the first.
schedule.quote: Write $\Xi_1$, $\Xi_2$ and $\Xi_3$ for three tape procedures.

schedule.name: third procedure
schedule.meaning: The third of three tape procedures in the example schedule, applied last.
schedule.quote: Write $\Xi_1$, $\Xi_2$ and $\Xi_3$ for three tape procedures.

schonhage-strassen.name: residue bit count
schonhage-strassen.meaning: The number of bits in a residue, which counts the binary digits of each residue.
schonhage-strassen.quote: Let $\vartheta$ be the number of bits in a residue.

schonhage-strassen.name: shift count
schonhage-strassen.meaning: The number of places by which a multiplication shifts the bits of a residue, which counts those places.
schonhage-strassen.quote: Let $\varsigma$ be the number of places a multiplication shifts, with $0\le\varsigma<\vartheta$.

schonhage-strassen.name: residue
schonhage-strassen.meaning: A residue, an integer from $0$ to $2^\vartheta-1$ whose bits are shifted.
schonhage-strassen.quote: Let $\Xi$ be a residue, with $0\le\Xi<2^\vartheta$, and write $\Xi=\sum_{\varpi=0}^{\vartheta-1}\Xi_\varpi 2^\varpi$, where $\varpi$ is a bit position from $0$ to $\vartheta-1$ and $\Xi_\varpi\in\{0,1\}$ is the bit of $\Xi$ at position $\varpi$.

schonhage-strassen.name: bit position
schonhage-strassen.meaning: The position of a bit of a residue, running from $0$ to $\vartheta-1$ with $0$ the least significant place.
schonhage-strassen.quote: Let $\Xi$ be a residue, with $0\le\Xi<2^\vartheta$, and write $\Xi=\sum_{\varpi=0}^{\vartheta-1}\Xi_\varpi 2^\varpi$, where $\varpi$ is a bit position from $0$ to $\vartheta-1$ and $\Xi_\varpi\in\{0,1\}$ is the bit of $\Xi$ at position $\varpi$.

schonhage-strassen.name: bit of a residue
schonhage-strassen.meaning: The bit of $\Xi$ at position $\varpi$, which is $0$ or $1$.
schonhage-strassen.quote: Let $\Xi$ be a residue, with $0\le\Xi<2^\vartheta$, and write $\Xi=\sum_{\varpi=0}^{\vartheta-1}\Xi_\varpi 2^\varpi$, where $\varpi$ is a bit position from $0$ to $\vartheta-1$ and $\Xi_\varpi\in\{0,1\}$ is the bit of $\Xi$ at position $\varpi$.

schoolbook-multiplication.name: bit position
schoolbook-multiplication.meaning: An integer from 0 to n-1 giving the position of a bit of y, counted from the least significant end.
schoolbook-multiplication.quote: For a position $\sigma$, an integer from $0$ to $n-1$ counted from the least significant end, let $y_\sigma \in \{0,1\}$ be the bit of $y$ there, so that $\mathrm{val}(y)=\sum_{\sigma=0}^{n-1} y_\sigma 2^\sigma$.

schoolbook-multiplication.name: bit of y
schoolbook-multiplication.meaning: The bit of y at position sigma, which is 0 or 1.
schoolbook-multiplication.quote: For a position $\sigma$, an integer from $0$ to $n-1$ counted from the least significant end, let $y_\sigma \in \{0,1\}$ be the bit of $y$ there, so that $\mathrm{val}(y)=\sum_{\sigma=0}^{n-1} y_\sigma 2^\sigma$.

schoolbook-multiplication.name: partial product
schoolbook-multiplication.meaning: The copy of x shifted left by sigma places when y_sigma is 1, and 0 when y_sigma is 0.
schoolbook-multiplication.quote: The partial product $\zeta_\sigma$ is the copy of $x$ shifted left by $\sigma$ places when $y_\sigma=1$, and $0$ when $y_\sigma=0$.

scratch-storage.name: control vector
scratch-storage.meaning: The control vector, with one entry $\phi_T$ for each triple $T$.
scratch-storage.quote: Write $\phi$ for the control vector, with entries $\phi_T$ at triples $T$, and $\mathcal{Y}$ for the target vector, with entries $\mathcal{Y}_S$.

scratch-storage.name: target vector
scratch-storage.meaning: The target vector, with one entry $\mathcal{Y}_S$ for each triple $S$.
scratch-storage.quote: Write $\phi$ for the control vector, with entries $\phi_T$ at triples $T$, and $\mathcal{Y}$ for the target vector, with entries $\mathcal{Y}_S$.

scratch-storage.name: triple
scratch-storage.meaning: A three-element subset of the ground set.
scratch-storage.quote: Write $S$ and $T$ for triples, which are three-element subsets of the ground set.

scratch-storage.name: triple
scratch-storage.meaning: A three-element subset of the ground set.
scratch-storage.quote: Write $S$ and $T$ for triples, which are three-element subsets of the ground set.

scratch-storage.name: starting side values
scratch-storage.meaning: The vector of starting values of the side wires $A_{ST}$.
scratch-storage.quote: Write $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ for the vectors of starting values of the side wires and of the central wires.

scratch-storage.name: starting central values
scratch-storage.meaning: The vector of starting values of the central wires $C_\ell$.
scratch-storage.quote: Write $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ for the vectors of starting values of the side wires and of the central wires.

scratch-storage.name: copy map
scratch-storage.meaning: The map that adds $\phi_T$ to the side wire $A_{ST}$ of each neighbouring pair.
scratch-storage.quote: $\mathcal{K}$ is copy, which adds $\phi_T$ to $A_{ST}$ for each neighbouring pair.

scratch-storage.name: side injection
scratch-storage.meaning: The map that adds to $\mathcal{Y}_S$ the side wires $A_{ST}$ over the neighbours $T$ of $S$.
scratch-storage.quote: $\mathcal{O}$ is side injection, which adds to $\mathcal{Y}_S$ the side wires $A_{ST}$ over the neighbours $T$ of $S$.

scratch-storage.name: gather map
scratch-storage.meaning: The map that adds $\phi_T$ to the central wire $C_\ell$ for each $\ell\in T$.
scratch-storage.quote: $\mathcal{Z}$ is gather, which adds $\phi_T$ to $C_\ell$ for each $\ell\in T$.

scratch-storage.name: scatter map
scratch-storage.meaning: The map that adds to $\mathcal{Y}_S$ the central wires $C_\ell$ with $\ell\in S$.
scratch-storage.quote: $\mathcal{R}$ is scatter, which adds to $\mathcal{Y}_S$ the central wires $C_\ell$ with $\ell\in S$.

signed-packing.name: integer polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: The first factor, an integer polynomial in $y$ with $r$ coefficients.
signed-packing.quote: Signed coefficient packing is based on the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md): $f$ and $g$ are integer polynomials, and their product is taken there.

signed-packing.name: integer polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: The second factor, an integer polynomial in $y$ with $r$ coefficients.
signed-packing.quote: Signed coefficient packing is based on the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md): $f$ and $g$ are integer polynomials, and their product is taken there.

signed-packing.name: coefficient of f
signed-packing.quote: Write $f = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} f_j y^j$ and $g = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} g_j y^j$, where $f_j$ and $g_j$ are the integer coefficients of $y^j$ in $f$ and $g$, for $j$ from $0$ to $r-1$.

signed-packing.name: coefficient of g
signed-packing.quote: Write $f = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} f_j y^j$ and $g = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} g_j y^j$, where $f_j$ and $g_j$ are the integer coefficients of $y^j$ in $f$ and $g$, for $j$ from $0$ to $r-1$.

signed-packing.name: coefficient bit bound
signed-packing.meaning: The number of bits in a bound on the coefficient magnitudes, so that each coefficient has absolute value at most $2^p$.
signed-packing.quote: Let $p$ be the number of bits in a bound on the coefficient magnitudes, so that $|f_j| \le 2^p$ and $|g_j| \le 2^p$ for all $j$.

signed-packing.name: ordinary product
signed-packing.meaning: The ordinary product $fg$ of the two integer polynomials.
signed-packing.quote: Substituting $B$ for $y$ respects products. The ordinary product of $f$ and $g$ is a polynomial $h = fg$ with at most $2r-1$ coefficients, where $h_j$ is the integer coefficient of $y^j$ in $h$, for $j$ from $0$ to $2r-2$.

signed-packing.name: coefficient of h
signed-packing.quote: Substituting $B$ for $y$ respects products. The ordinary product of $f$ and $g$ is a polynomial $h = fg$ with at most $2r-1$ coefficients, where $h_j$ is the integer coefficient of $y^j$ in $h$, for $j$ from $0$ to $2r-2$.

signed-packing.name: block base
signed-packing.meaning: The block base $2^{4p}$, the value substituted for $y$ and the modulus of the congruence used for recovery.
signed-packing.quote: Packing fixes the block base $B = 2^{4p}$ and replaces $y$ by $B$.

signed-packing.name: centered residue
signed-packing.meaning: The unique integer in $[-B/2, B/2)$ congruent to $f(B)\,g(B)$ modulo $B$.
signed-packing.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the unique integer in $[-B/2, B/2)$ with $f(B)\,g(B) \equiv \sigma \pmod B$, the centered residue of $f(B)\,g(B)$ modulo $B$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: number of axes
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of transform axes that the layer acts on, one selected bit on each.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The layer acts on $D$ [transform axes](transform-axis.md), where $D$ is the number of axes.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: chunk width
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of consecutive address bits in each transform axis (chunk).
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Each axis is a chunk of $\delta$ consecutive address bits, where $\delta$ is the number of bits in each chunk.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: selected offset
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The position of the selected bit within its chunk, counted from the least significant end.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: In each chunk one bit is selected, at the same offset $o$ with $0\le o<\delta$, where $o$ is the position of the selected bit within its chunk, counted from the least significant end.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: two-point map
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The two-point map $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$, as a $2\times2$ matrix.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Write $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ for the two-point map, whose matrix is $H_0=\frac12\left(\begin{array}{cc}1&1\\1&-1\end{array}\right)$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: length-q transform
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform on $q$ values, normalized by $1/q$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: number of values
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of values that the transform $F_q$ acts on.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: input index
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The index of an input value in the transform $F_q$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: output index
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The index of an output coordinate of the transform $F_q$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: normalized Hadamard matrix
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The $2\times2$ Hadamard matrix with the $1/\sqrt2$ normalization.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The unitary normalization $1/\sqrt q$ gives the normalized Hadamard matrix $\mathcal H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(\begin{array}{cc}1&1\\1&-1\end{array}\right)=\sqrt2\,H_0$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: diagonal phase matrix
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(1,i)$ be a diagonal phase matrix, $X=\left(\begin{array}{cc}0&1\\1&0\end{array}\right)$ the bit-flip matrix, and $I$ the $2\times2$ identity matrix.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: bit-flip matrix
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The $2\times2$ matrix that swaps the two basis states of one bit.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(1,i)$ be a diagonal phase matrix, $X=\left(\begin{array}{cc}0&1\\1&0\end{array}\right)$ the bit-flip matrix, and $I$ the $2\times2$ identity matrix.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: identity matrix
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(1,i)$ be a diagonal phase matrix, $X=\left(\begin{array}{cc}0&1\\1&0\end{array}\right)$ the bit-flip matrix, and $I$ the $2\times2$ identity matrix.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: identity coefficient
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The coefficient of $I$ in $C$, equal to $(1+i)/2$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $\lambda=(1+i)/2$ and $\mu=(1-i)/2$, where $\lambda$ is the coefficient of the identity $I$ and $\mu$ the coefficient of $X$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: bit-flip coefficient
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The coefficient of $X$ in $C$, equal to $(1-i)/2$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $\lambda=(1+i)/2$ and $\mu=(1-i)/2$, where $\lambda$ is the coefficient of the identity $I$ and $\mu$ the coefficient of $X$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: two-point kernel
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The two-by-two operator $\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H$, equal to $\lambda I+\mu X$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Define $C=\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H$, which equals $\lambda I+\mu X$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: address phase operator
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The diagonal operator $\Delta^{\otimes D}$ that multiplies each address by $i$ to the number of selected bits equal to 1 there.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $\Delta_D=\Delta^{\otimes D}$ multiplies the value at each address by $i$ raised to the number of selected bits equal to 1 there, so $\Delta_D$ is diagonal.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: working precision
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The working precision in bits: the inputs lie on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $p$ is the working precision in bits.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: number of H_0 factors
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of individual factors $H_0$ applied, which refines the grid to $2^{-(p+s)}$.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $s$ changes meaning and counts the individual factors $H_0$ applied.

stable-radix-sort.name: record count
stable-radix-sort.meaning: The number of records in the full stream, a count of records, so every rank is an integer from 0 to M-1.
stable-radix-sort.quote: Let $M$ be the number of records in the full stream, and let $w$ be the number of bits in each key.

stable-radix-sort.name: key width
stable-radix-sort.meaning: The number of bits in each key, a count of bits, which is also the number of passes.
stable-radix-sort.quote: Let $M$ be the number of records in the full stream, and let $w$ be the number of bits in each key.

stable-radix-sort.name: record key
stable-radix-sort.meaning: The key of a record, a string of w bits written as q_{w-1} through q_0.
stable-radix-sort.quote: Write a key as $q = q_{w-1}\cdots q_0$, where $q_t \in \{0,1\}$ is its bit of weight $2^t$ at each bit position $t$ from $0$ to $w-1$.

stable-radix-sort.name: key bit
stable-radix-sort.meaning: The bit of the key at position t, which is 0 or 1 and has weight 2^t.
stable-radix-sort.quote: Write a key as $q = q_{w-1}\cdots q_0$, where $q_t \in \{0,1\}$ is its bit of weight $2^t$ at each bit position $t$ from $0$ to $w-1$.

stable-radix-sort.name: bit position
stable-radix-sort.meaning: A bit position of the key, counted from 0 at the least significant bit, which also indexes the pass that sorts by that bit.
stable-radix-sort.quote: Write a key as $q = q_{w-1}\cdots q_0$, where $q_t \in \{0,1\}$ is its bit of weight $2^t$ at each bit position $t$ from $0$ to $w-1$.

stable-radix-sort.name: size parameter
stable-radix-sort.meaning: The paper's size parameter for its integers, which bounds the number of bits in the destination keys.
stable-radix-sort.quote: Here $A_{\mathrm{rect}}$ is the paper's size parameter for its integers.

standard-basis-vector.name: standard basis vector
standard-basis-vector.meaning: The vector of $F^m$ with entry $1$ at coordinate $j$ and $0$ at every other coordinate.
standard-basis-vector.quote: For each coordinate $j$ with $1\le j\le m$, the standard basis vector $\sigma_j$ is the vector of $F^m$ with entry $1$ at coordinate $j$ and $0$ at every other coordinate.

subset-intersection-network.name: ground set size
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The number of elements of the ground set $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$, a count.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, whose size is $h$.

subset-intersection-network.name: triples
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of the ground set.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of all triples.

subset-intersection-network.name: triple S
subset-intersection-network.meaning: A triple, one of the letters that always denote triples on this page.
subset-intersection-network.quote: The letters $S$ and $T$ always denote three-element subsets of $[h]$, called *triples*.

subset-intersection-network.name: triple T
subset-intersection-network.meaning: A triple, one of the letters that always denote triples on this page.
subset-intersection-network.quote: The letters $S$ and $T$ always denote three-element subsets of $[h]$, called *triples*.

subset-intersection-network.name: bank index
subset-intersection-network.meaning: A triple of triples $(\Psi_1,\Psi_2,\Psi_3)$ that indexes one entry of a bank.
subset-intersection-network.quote: A *bank* is a family of scalars indexed by $\Psi=(\Psi_1,\Psi_2,\Psi_3)\in\mathcal T^3$.

subset-intersection-network.name: source bank
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The bank of scalars that the exchange reads from.
subset-intersection-network.quote: The network has two banks $X$ and $Y$, with entries $X_\Psi$ and $Y_\Psi$.

subset-intersection-network.name: target bank
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The bank of scalars that the exchange writes to.
subset-intersection-network.quote: The network has two banks $X$ and $Y$, with entries $X_\Psi$ and $Y_\Psi$.

subset-intersection-network.name: side wire
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The wire attached to an ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each ground element $\Upsilon\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\Upsilon$.

subset-intersection-network.name: central wire
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The wire attached to a ground element $\Upsilon$.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each ground element $\Upsilon\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\Upsilon$.

subset-intersection-network.name: ground element
subset-intersection-network.meaning: An element of the ground set $[h]$, which indexes a central wire.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each ground element $\Upsilon\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\Upsilon$.

subset-intersection-network.name: starting side values
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The starting values of the side wires, which the network must restore.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Let $A^0$ and $C^0$ be the starting values of the side wires and the central wires.

subset-intersection-network.name: starting central values
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The starting values of the central wires, which the network must restore.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Let $A^0$ and $C^0$ be the starting values of the side wires and the central wires.

subset-intersection-network.name: indicator vector
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The $0/1$ vector in $E$ whose ones mark the three elements of $T$.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Let $t_T$ be the $0/1$ indicator vector of $T$.

subset-intersection-network.name: bilinear space
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The fixed bilinear space whose subspaces are the labels; the letter $E$ changes meaning here.
subset-intersection-network.quote: The network labels its wires with [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space $E$.

subset-intersection-network.name: all-ones matrix
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The $h\times h$ matrix whose entries are all $1$.
subset-intersection-network.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

subset-intersection-network.name: first form vector
subset-intersection-network.meaning: A vector of $E$ in the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle$.
subset-intersection-network.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

subset-intersection-network.name: second form vector
subset-intersection-network.meaning: A vector of $E$ in the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle$.
subset-intersection-network.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

subspace-labels.name: fixed space
subspace-labels.meaning: The fixed space in which the labels are nondegenerate subspaces, carrying a bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Write $E$ for the fixed space, and $\xi$ and $\eta$ for vectors of $E$.

subspace-labels.name: label
subspace-labels.meaning: A label, a nondegenerate subspace of $E$ attached to the wires of the network.
subspace-labels.quote: Labels take their orthogonality from its [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle$, and $\mathcal L$ denotes a label, a nondegenerate subspace of $E$.

subspace-labels.name: smaller label
subspace-labels.meaning: The smaller of the two labels on an edge, contained in the larger.
subspace-labels.quote: Write $\mathcal L$ for the larger label of an edge and $\mathcal L'\subseteq\mathcal L$ for the smaller.

subspace-labels.name: label frame
subspace-labels.meaning: The invertible operator on arrays carried by a vertex with label $\mathcal L$.
subspace-labels.quote: so a vertex with label $\mathcal L$ carries the frame $C_{\mathcal L}$

subspace-labels.name: Hadamard matrix
subspace-labels.meaning: The Hadamard matrix of order 2, the one-bit building block of the frame.
subspace-labels.quote: Let $\mathcal H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the Hadamard matrix of order 2, so $\mathcal H^2=I$

subspace-labels.name: diagonal operator
subspace-labels.meaning: The diagonal operator on functions of $x$ that multiplies the value at each address by its displayed power of $i$.
subspace-labels.quote: $\mathrm{diag}_x$ is the diagonal operator that multiplies the value at each address $x$ by $i^{\,\mathrm{hw}(\Theta_{\mathcal L}x)\bmod 4}$

subspace-labels.name: Hamming weight
subspace-labels.meaning: The number of ones in a binary vector.
subspace-labels.quote: For a binary vector $z$, $\mathrm{hw}(z)$ is its Hamming weight, the number of ones.

subspace-labels.name: vector of E
subspace-labels.meaning: An arbitrary vector of the fixed space $E$, the first argument of the bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Write $E$ for the fixed space, and $\xi$ and $\eta$ for vectors of $E$.

subspace-labels.name: vector of E
subspace-labels.meaning: An arbitrary vector of the fixed space $E$, the second argument of the bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Write $E$ for the fixed space, and $\xi$ and $\eta$ for vectors of $E$.

subspace-labels.name: translation
subspace-labels.meaning: The map that shifts a function's argument by the binary vector $v$; the letter $X$ changes meaning here.
subspace-labels.quote: Let $X_v$ be the translation $(X_vf)(x)=f(x+v)$ for a binary vector $v\in\mathbb F_2^m$; here $v$ is a binary vector, not a vertex, and $X$ is not the bit flip of other pages.

supremum.name: set of reals
supremum.meaning: A nonempty set of real numbers, whose upper bounds and supremum are taken.
supremum.quote: Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty set of real numbers.

supremum.name: set element
supremum.meaning: An arbitrary element of the set $\Sigma$, compared with a candidate upper bound.
supremum.quote: Let $\chi$ denote an arbitrary element of $\Sigma$.

supremum.name: candidate bound
supremum.meaning: A real number, tested as a candidate upper bound of the set.

supremum.name: positive integer index
supremum.meaning: A positive integer index labeling the elements $1-2^{-\nu}$ of the example set.
supremum.quote:
Take $\Sigma = \{\,1-2^{-
u} : 
u \ge 1\,\} = \{1/2, 3/4, 7/8, \dots\}$, where $
u$ is a positive integer index.

supremum.name: gap below one
supremum.meaning: The positive real number $1-\Omega$, the gap between $\Omega$ and $1$.
supremum.quote: Let $\Omega < 1$, and let $\varepsilon = 1-\Omega > 0$ be the gap between $\Omega$ and $1$.

supremum.name: linear map
supremum.meaning: A linear map, that is, a map preserving sums and scalar multiples, whose operator norm is taken.
supremum.quote: For a linear map $T$, meaning a map that preserves sums and scalar multiples, the largest factor by which $T$ stretches a vector is its operator norm $\|T\|$.

supremum.name: operator norm
supremum.meaning: The largest factor by which the linear map $T$ stretches a vector, defined as a supremum over inputs of array norm at most one.
supremum.quote: For a linear map $T$, meaning a map that preserves sums and scalar multiples, the largest factor by which $T$ stretches a vector is its operator norm $\|T\|$.

supremum.name: input vector
supremum.meaning: One input vector, a finite list of complex numbers, to which the linear map is applied.
supremum.quote: Here $v$ denotes one input vector, a finite list of complex numbers, and $\|v\|$ denotes its largest modulus (absolute value) over all entries.

symmetric-matrix.name: transpose
symmetric-matrix.meaning: The transpose of the matrix $A$, whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is $A_{ji}$.
symmetric-matrix.quote: The *transpose* $A^{\top}$ of an $m\times m$ matrix $A$ is the $m\times m$ matrix whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is $A_{ji}$, so its rows are the columns of $A$.

synthetic-transforms.name: polynomial ring
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The ring $R_r$ of polynomials in $y$ with complex coefficients in which $y^r = -1$.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Write $R_r = \mathbb{C}[y]/(y^r+1)$ for the ring of polynomials in the variable $y$ with complex coefficients, in which $y^r$ is identified with $-1$.

synthetic-transforms.name: coefficient position
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The position of a coefficient in a record, running from 0 to r minus 1.
synthetic-transforms.quote: A record is an element of $R_r$, stored as its $r$ coefficients $c_\varrho$, where $\varrho$, the coefficient position, runs from $0$ to $r-1$ and $c_\varrho$ multiplies $y^\varrho$.

synthetic-transforms.name: shift count
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The number of places a shift moves each coefficient, a value from 0 up to 2r minus 1.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Let $\xi$, with $0 \le \xi < 2r$, be the shift count, the number of places a shift moves each coefficient.

synthetic-transforms.name: wrap count
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The number of times a shift carries the coefficient at position rho past the end of the record.
synthetic-transforms.quote: For position $\varrho$, let $\mu_\varrho = \lfloor (\varrho+\xi)/r \rfloor$ be the wrap count: the number of times the shift carries the coefficient past position $r-1$, where $\lfloor x \rfloor$ is the largest integer not exceeding $x$.

synthetic-transforms.name: polynomial root of unity
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The element $y^{2r/N}$ of $R_r$, a primitive N-th root of unity.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Write $\omega_N = y^{2r/N}$ for the polynomial root of unity; it is the polynomial counterpart of the complex root $\omega$ of the Fourier transform, and a [root of unity](root-of-unity.md) of order $N$ in $R_r$.

synthetic-transforms.name: entry index
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The index of an entry of a transform's input list, running from 0 to N minus 1.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Let $N$ be a power of two dividing $2r$, the number of entries in a transform, and let $\upsilon$, running from $0$ to $N-1$, be the entry index that numbers the entries.

synthetic-transforms.name: input list
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The list of N records that a transform takes as input.
synthetic-transforms.quote: The input is $P=(P_0,\dots,P_{N-1})$, a list of $N$ records, and $P_\upsilon$ is its $\upsilon$-th entry.

synthetic-transforms.name: output list
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The transformed list of N records that a transform returns.
synthetic-transforms.quote: The output is $\hat P=(\hat P_0,\dots,\hat P_{N-1})$, the transformed list, where $\zeta$, the output index, runs from $0$ to $N-1$:

synthetic-transforms.name: output index
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The index of an entry of the output list, running from 0 to N minus 1.
synthetic-transforms.quote: The output is $\hat P=(\hat P_0,\dots,\hat P_{N-1})$, the transformed list, where $\zeta$, the output index, runs from $0$ to $N-1$:

synthetic-transforms.name: half-block size
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The number of positions in each half of a block at a level, a power of two from 1 to N/2.
synthetic-transforms.quote: The levels run with half-block size $\vartheta$, the number of positions in each half of a block, taking the values $1,2,4,\dots,N/2$.

synthetic-transforms.name: block offset
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The position of a butterfly within the first half of its block, from 0 to half-block size minus 1.
synthetic-transforms.quote: For each block offset $\varpi$ from $0$ to $\vartheta-1$, the pair at positions $\varpi$ and $\varpi+\vartheta$ of the block is replaced by

synthetic-transforms.name: twiddle
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The power of the polynomial root of unity that multiplies W in a butterfly.
synthetic-transforms.quote: where $\theta = \omega_N^{\varpi N/(2\vartheta)}$ is the twiddle of that butterfly, the power of $\omega_N$ that multiplies $W$:

synthetic-transforms.name: butterfly entry U
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The entry of a butterfly pair at the lower position.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Each butterfly takes a pair of entries, $U$ at the lower position and $W$ at the upper position of the pair.

synthetic-transforms.name: butterfly entry W
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The entry of a butterfly pair at the upper position, multiplied by the twiddle.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Each butterfly takes a pair of entries, $U$ at the lower position and $W$ at the upper position of the pair.

tape-procedure.name: chunk count bound
tape-procedure.meaning: An upper bound on the number of equal-width address chunks whose selected bits one pass handles.
tape-procedure.quote: Here the letter $d$ changes meaning: it bounds the number of equal-width address chunks that one pass handles.

telescoping-identity.name: last index
telescoping-identity.meaning: The index of the last term of the sequence, so that the sequence has o+1 terms.
telescoping-identity.quote: Let $o$ be the index of the last term, so the sequence has $o+1$ terms.

telescoping-identity.name: term position
telescoping-identity.meaning: The position of a term in the sequence, running from 0 to o.
telescoping-identity.quote: The index $k$ is the position of a term, running from $0$ to $o$.

telescoping-identity.name: term at position k
telescoping-identity.meaning: The number at position k of the sequence.
telescoping-identity.quote: The term $\iota_k$ is the number at position $k$, so the sequence is $\iota_0,\iota_1,\dots,\iota_o$.

telescoping-identity.name: list of numbers
telescoping-identity.meaning: A list of numbers indexed by position k, whose entry at position k is x_k.
telescoping-identity.quote: For a list $x$ of numbers, $x_k$ is the entry at position $k$.

telescoping-identity.name: first position
telescoping-identity.meaning: The first position of a sum over positions, the lower limit of the sum.
telescoping-identity.quote: The sum $\sum_{k=s}^{e} x_k$ stands for $x_s+x_{s+1}+\dots+x_e$, where $s$ is the first position and $e$ the last, and it is $0$ when $e<s$.

telescoping-identity.name: last position
telescoping-identity.meaning: The last position of a sum over positions, the upper limit of the sum.
telescoping-identity.quote: The sum $\sum_{k=s}^{e} x_k$ stands for $x_s+x_{s+1}+\dots+x_e$, where $s$ is the first position and $e$ the last, and it is $0$ when $e<s$.

tensor-product.name: matrix P
tensor-product.meaning: A matrix whose entries $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ are indexed by its rows and columns.
tensor-product.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix with rows indexed by $\upsilon$ and columns indexed by $\varrho$, so $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\varrho$.

tensor-product.name: matrix Q
tensor-product.meaning: A second matrix whose entries $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ are indexed by its rows and columns.
tensor-product.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix with rows indexed by $\varpi$ and columns indexed by $\varsigma$, so $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ is its entry in row $\varpi$ and column $\varsigma$.

tensor-product.name: row index of P
tensor-product.meaning: The row index of the matrix $P$, running over its rows.
tensor-product.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix with rows indexed by $\upsilon$ and columns indexed by $\varrho$, so $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\varrho$.

tensor-product.name: column index of P
tensor-product.meaning: The column index of the matrix $P$, running over its columns.
tensor-product.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix with rows indexed by $\upsilon$ and columns indexed by $\varrho$, so $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\varrho$.

tensor-product.name: row index of Q
tensor-product.meaning: The row index of the matrix $Q$, running over its rows.
tensor-product.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix with rows indexed by $\varpi$ and columns indexed by $\varsigma$, so $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ is its entry in row $\varpi$ and column $\varsigma$.

tensor-product.name: column index of Q
tensor-product.meaning: The column index of the matrix $Q$, running over its columns.
tensor-product.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix with rows indexed by $\varpi$ and columns indexed by $\varsigma$, so $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ is its entry in row $\varpi$ and column $\varsigma$.

tensor-product.name: factor count
tensor-product.meaning: The number of factors of a tensor power, which is also the number of coordinates it acts on.
tensor-product.quote: The $\Upsilon$-fold tensor power, where $\Upsilon\ge 1$ is a count, the number of factors and of coordinates acted on, is defined by $P^{\otimes 1}=P$ and $P^{\otimes\Upsilon}=P\otimes P^{\otimes(\Upsilon-1)}$.

tensor-product.name: second matrix P'
tensor-product.meaning: A matrix of a size compatible with $P$, used in the mixed-product rule.
tensor-product.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

tensor-product.name: second matrix Q'
tensor-product.meaning: A matrix of a size compatible with $Q$, used in the mixed-product rule.
tensor-product.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

tensor-product.name: column index of P'
tensor-product.meaning: The column index of the matrix $P'$, running over its columns.
tensor-product.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

tensor-product.name: column index of Q'
tensor-product.meaning: The column index of the matrix $Q'$, running over its columns.
tensor-product.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

tensor-product.name: coordinate position
tensor-product.meaning: The position of one of the $\Upsilon$ coordinates, numbered from 1 to $\Upsilon$.
tensor-product.quote: For a coordinate position $\phi$ with $1\le\phi\le\Upsilon$, let $P_{(\phi)}$ apply $P$ to coordinate $\phi$ and the identity to the others, so $P_{(\phi)}=I\otimes\cdots\otimes P\otimes\cdots\otimes I$ with $P$ in place $\phi$.

tensor-product.name: single-coordinate operator
tensor-product.meaning: The operator that applies $P$ to coordinate $\phi$ and the identity to the other coordinates.
tensor-product.quote: For a coordinate position $\phi$ with $1\le\phi\le\Upsilon$, let $P_{(\phi)}$ apply $P$ to coordinate $\phi$ and the identity to the others, so $P_{(\phi)}=I\otimes\cdots\otimes P\otimes\cdots\otimes I$ with $P$ in place $\phi$.

transform-axis.name: number of axes
transform-axis.meaning: The number of axes of the array.
transform-axis.quote: Let $D$ be the number of axes.

transform-axis.name: axis index
transform-axis.meaning: The index of one axis, running from 1 to D.
transform-axis.quote: Let $\mu$ be the index of one axis, $1 \le \mu \le D$.

transform-axis.name: axis length
transform-axis.meaning: The number of values the coordinate along axis mu takes.
transform-axis.quote: Let $\theta_\mu$ be the length of axis $\mu$, the number of values its coordinate takes.

transform-axis.name: axis coordinate
transform-axis.meaning: The coordinate of an address along axis mu, an integer from 0 to theta_mu minus 1.
transform-axis.quote: Let $\xi_\mu$ be the coordinate of an address along axis $\mu$, so $0 \le \xi_\mu < \theta_\mu$.

transform-axis.name: coefficient count
transform-axis.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in one stored polynomial, a power of two.
transform-axis.quote: Let $P$ be the number of complex coefficients in one stored polynomial, a power of two.

transform-axis.name: stored coefficient
transform-axis.meaning: The coefficient of y to the power k in the stored polynomial.
transform-axis.quote: Modulo $y^P+1$ means $y^P$ is replaced by $-1$, so the stored form is $\phi_0+\phi_1y+\dots+\phi_{P-1}y^{P-1}$, where $\phi_k$ is the coefficient of $y^k$.

transform-axis.name: transform length
transform-axis.meaning: A power of two, at least 2, that divides 2P and is the length of a transform axis.
transform-axis.quote: Let $\varrho \ge 2$ be a power of two dividing $2P$, the length of a transform axis.

transform-axis.name: axis root
transform-axis.meaning: The root of unity y to the power 2P divided by rho, which has order rho.
transform-axis.quote: Let $\zeta=y^{2P/\varrho}$, a root of unity of order $\varrho$.

transform-identity.name: Fourier transform
transform-identity.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $s$, applied to vectors of length $s$.
transform-identity.quote: Here $F_s$ is the normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $s$, $(F_su)_k=\frac1s\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}u_je^{-2\pi ijk/s}$, and $F_t$ is the one of length $t$.

transform-identity.name: Fourier transform
transform-identity.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $t$.
transform-identity.quote: Here $F_s$ is the normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $s$, $(F_su)_k=\frac1s\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}u_je^{-2\pi ijk/s}$, and $F_t$ is the one of length $t$.

transform-identity.name: coordinate permutation
transform-identity.meaning: A permutation that rearranges the entries of a vector by their positions.
transform-identity.quote: For a coordinate permutation $\Pi$, which rearranges entries by position,

transform-identity.name: retained permutation
transform-identity.meaning: The permutation of entries of a length-$s$ vector that sends position $j$ to position $cj$ modulo $s$.
transform-identity.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $s$ (the letter $c$ changes meaning here), the retained permutation $\Pi_c$ sends $z$ to the vector with $(\Pi_cz)_j=z_{cj}$, indices taken modulo $s$.

transform-identity.name: unit multiplier
transform-identity.meaning: A unit modulo $s$ that defines the retained permutation $\Pi_c$.
transform-identity.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $s$ (the letter $c$ changes meaning here), the retained permutation $\Pi_c$ sends $z$ to the vector with $(\Pi_cz)_j=z_{cj}$, indices taken modulo $s$.

transform-identity.name: inverse of t
transform-identity.meaning: An integer with $\chi t\equiv 1 \pmod s$, so it inverts $t$ modulo $s$.
transform-identity.quote: By [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) there is an integer $\chi$ with $\chi t\equiv 1 \pmod s$ (the letter $\chi$ changes meaning here).

transform-identity.name: second position
transform-identity.meaning: A second position in $\{0,\dots,s-1\}$, compared with $j$.
transform-identity.quote: If $tj\equiv tj'\pmod s$ for positions $j,j'$ in $\{0,\dots,s-1\}$, multiplying by $\chi$ gives $j\equiv j'$, so $j\mapsto tj$ is one-to-one, hence a permutation.

transform-identity.name: second vector
transform-identity.meaning: A second vector of length $s$, paired with $u$ in a pointwise product.
transform-identity.quote: For vectors $u,u'$, the pointwise product $u\cdot u'$ has entries $u_ju'_j$.

transform-identity.name: linear contraction
transform-identity.meaning: A linear map from $\mathbb{C}^s$ to $\mathbb{C}^t$ in the lemma.
transform-identity.quote: $A$ maps $\mathbb{C}^s$ to $\mathbb{C}^t$ and $B_0$ maps back (here $A$ changes meaning from the machine of other pages).

transform-identity.name: linear contraction
transform-identity.meaning: A linear map from $\mathbb{C}^t$ to $\mathbb{C}^s$ in the lemma.
transform-identity.quote: $A$ maps $\mathbb{C}^s$ to $\mathbb{C}^t$ and $B_0$ maps back (here $A$ changes meaning from the machine of other pages).

transform-identity.name: generic linear map
transform-identity.meaning: A generic linear map, used to define contractions.
transform-identity.quote: A linear map $\Psi$ is a contraction when $\|\Psi u\|\le\|u\|$, where $\|u\|$ is the largest modulus of an entry of $u$.

transform-identity.name: relative gap
transform-identity.meaning: The ratio $t/s$ minus one, which the lemma requires to exceed $p/\alpha^4$.
transform-identity.quote: Write $\theta=t/s-1$ (the letter $\theta$ changes meaning here).

transform-identity.name: left inverse of Gamma
transform-identity.meaning: A linear map with $\Upsilon\Gamma=I$, built from $N^{-1}$ and a diagonal scaling.
transform-identity.quote: The proof builds its left inverse from a [diagonal scaling](diagonal-scaling.md) and $N^{-1}$ and a coordinate selection: a linear map $\Upsilon$ with $\Upsilon\Gamma=I$.

transform-layout.name: transform layout
transform-layout.meaning: The permutation of record addresses that places the selected bits of the participating axes at one common offset.
transform-layout.quote: The transform layout $\mathcal{L}$ is an explicit [permutation](permutation.md) of record addresses.

transform-layout.name: participating axis count
transform-layout.meaning: The number of participating axes of a round, which is the number of chunks that share one offset.
transform-layout.quote: Here $D$ is the number of participating axes, and $K$ is the number of bits in each chunk; $K$ has other meanings on earlier pages.

transform-layout.name: chunk width
transform-layout.meaning: The number of consecutive address bits in each chunk.
transform-layout.quote: Here $D$ is the number of participating axes, and $K$ is the number of bits in each chunk; $K$ has other meanings on earlier pages.

transform-layout.name: chunk offset
transform-layout.meaning: The position of the selected bit within its chunk, counted from the least significant end.
transform-layout.quote: Here $\upsilon$ is that offset, the position of the selected bit within its chunk, with $0\le\upsilon<K$.

transform-layout.name: round bit position
transform-layout.meaning: The position, counted from the least significant end, of the bit on which a round acts.
transform-layout.quote: A round on the bit at position $\varsigma$, counted from the least significant end, with $(\lg r-1)\bmod K\le\varsigma\le\lg r-2$, selects offset $(\varsigma-((\lg r-1)\bmod K))\bmod K$ within its chunk.

transform-round.name: participating axis count
transform-round.meaning: The number of participating axes, the axes that take a butterfly step in the round.
transform-round.quote: Let $D$ be the number of participating axes, and let $i$ index them (the letter $i$ changes meaning here).

binary-field.quote: The addition of $\mathbb{F}_2$ is defined by [Congruence](congruence-modulo.md) modulo $2$.

bit-network.quote: The bit network is a binary instance of [linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md), since its wires carry scalars of $\mathbb{F}_2$, the field with two elements in which addition is exclusive or and multiplication is AND.
The bit network realises a [binary change of basis](binary-change-of-basis.md) on tape by interchanging equal address chunks.

bit-procedure.quote: It performs an [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md) by a shear over the binary field, and the recursion in [Rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md) uses it as a cheap field interchange.

The bit procedure counts its interchanges by the [matrix rank](matrix-rank.md) of each edge matrix.

bit-reversed-order.quote: The order reverses the bits of each [Address](address.md) $\alpha$ to find the slot that stores its entry.

bluestein-chirp-identity.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_q$ of even length $q$ as a convolution multiplied by chirp factors.
It reduces the transform to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), so any method that computes that convolution also computes the transform.
The identity is applied inside the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), which keeps the permutations in the formula.

In the argument it turns the [middle transform](middle-transform.md), including its target permutation, into a [normalized cyclic convolution](normalized-cyclic-convolution.md), which the paper's convolution method can compute.
The identity gives its cost with the [logarithm](logarithm.md) $\lg q$, the exponent to which $2$ must be raised to give $q$: if the convolution costs $O(q\lg q)$ steps, so does the transform.
For even $q$ the wrap-around carries no sign, so the identity avoids a [negacyclic convolution](negacyclic-convolution.md), a convolution in which a wrap-around picks up a minus sign.

butterfly.quote: The butterfly is an elementary step of the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md).
The butterfly is followed by a [Cyclic shift](cyclic-shift.md) of each record.

carry-propagation.quote: Carry propagation takes its input from [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md).
Carry propagation takes its digit width from the [base-2 logarithm](base-two-logarithm.md) of $n$: $b = \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$.
Carry propagation computes its digit count by the [ceiling function](ceiling-function.md): $J = \lceil n/b \rceil$.

ceiling-function.quote: The ceiling rounds up recovered coefficients on the way to the binary product of [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md).

centered-residue.quote: The centered residue of an integer $\nu$ modulo $B$ is the representative of a residue class of [Congruence](congruence-modulo.md) modulo $B$ that lies in $[-B/2, B/2)$, so a small negative integer keeps its sign.

centered-residue.predicate: reads each coefficient back out of
centered-residue.quote: The centered residue reads each coefficient back out of a [Signed coefficient packing](signed-packing.md) one step at a time.

chinese-remainder-map.quote: The Chinese-remainder map relabels the positions of a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md).
It places the coefficients of a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) on distinct prime cyclic axes.
The map labels each position by its [mixed-radix digits](mixed-radix-digits.md) for the axis lengths.

chinese-remainder-map.predicate: is extended to polynomials as a
chinese-remainder-map.quote: The map is extended to polynomials as a [ring homomorphism](ring-homomorphism.md), a map that preserves sums and products.

chinese-remainder-theorem.quote: The Chinese remainder theorem says when a system of [congruences](congruence-modulo.md) has a solution, and how many solutions it has.
The theorem requires moduli that are pairwise [coprime](coprime.md).

complex-construction.quote: The complex construction is a variant of the [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) that takes its scalars from [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), so that it exchanges two banks of values exactly.

The complex construction is a variant of the [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) that takes its scalars from [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), so that it exchanges two banks of values exactly.
The complex construction reads its overlaps from [Indicator vector](indicator-vector.md)s, since $|S\cap T|=t_S^{\mathsf T}t_T$, where $t_S$ is the indicator vector of $S$.
The complex construction changes the neighbour rule of the [Bit construction](bit-construction.md) and keeps its copy step.

complex-phase-network.quote: The complex phase network is built on the [subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md), with each wire carrying an array of complex values instead of a scalar.
The complex phase network has coefficients in [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), since each such entry is a Gaussian integer divided by $2^m$.
The complex phase network is indexed by [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md).
The complex phase network takes its addresses from the [binary field](binary-field.md), in which addition is exclusive or.

The complex phase network computes its frames by the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) $H^{\otimes m}$ of $H=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, the normalized Hadamard matrix; here $H$ denotes this matrix, not the address chunk of other pages.
The complex phase network checks nondegeneracy with the [Gram matrix](gram-matrix.md) of each label, the matrix of dot products of a basis of $U$.

congruence-modulo.quote: Congruence is defined on pairs of [Integer](integer.md) values, and it groups them by their remainder after division by a fixed positive integer.
Congruence is applied in [Carry propagation](carry-propagation.md): each output digit is the residue of the input coefficient plus the incoming carry.

convolution.quote: Convolution is the computation behind [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md), which the method below relies on.

coprime.predicate: lets cyclic axes combine into one
coprime.quote: Coprimality of the lengths lets several cyclic axes combine into one [transform axis](transform-axis.md) of their product length.

cost-table.quote: The cost table splits the [running time cost](running-time-cost.md) of the algorithm into separate terms, one per kind of work.
The second row bounds the cost of the chunk exchanges that produce the [transform layout](transform-layout.md).
The first row prices moves to their [destination rank](destination-rank.md), which use $O(dK)$ linear scans.
The third row prices each simultaneous [butterfly round](transform-round.md), which acts on all axes at once.

The fourth row bounds the cost of the axis exposure and restoration around the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) step: $O(d^2)$ axis moves of cost $O(\Upsilon(1+\ell^{\tau}))$ each.
The fifth row bounds the cost of the line maps of [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
It divides every term by the [logical bit volume](logical-bit-volume.md) $\Upsilon$ of the box, so each term becomes a power of $p$ once $d$, $K$ and $\ell$ are substituted.

cyclic-convolution.quote: A cyclic convolution of length $n$ is split by the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) into a $D$-dimensional cyclic convolution when $n = n_1 \cdots n_D$ with $n_1, \dots, n_D$ pairwise coprime (no common factor above 1).
The layout relies on a [Modular inverse](modular-inverse.md) modulo $n_\kappa$ for each multiplier $\mu_\kappa$, which is a positive integer.

cyclic-coordinate.quote: A cyclic coordinate is one axis of a multidimensional [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), with its own cyclic length.

cyclic-group.quote: The cyclic group here is based on [Coprime](coprime.md) integers: $\langle\upsilon\rangle$ has order $W$, the product of the pairwise coprime family $f_1,\dots,f_J$.

cyclic-shift.quote: A controlled cyclic shift rotates the values of a target [address field](address-field.md) whose offset is set by control bits before it.

destination-rank.quote: Each destination rank is the key on which the extracted records are sorted by [Stable radix sort](stable-radix-sort.md).

destination-rank.predicate: is computed by a scan of
destination-rank.quote: The destination rank is computed by a scan of the [Stream](stream.md) in order, with a counter.

diagonal-scaling.quote: A diagonal scaling is built from the linear maps of [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).

discrete-fourier-transform.quote: The discrete Fourier transform is needed for [convolution](convolution.md).

dual-space.quote: The dual space $U^*$ collects every [Linear functional](linear-functional.md) on $U$ into one vector space.

The endpoint operator is instantiated by the [bit procedure](bit-procedure.md).
The endpoint operator of the bit procedure is implemented by [field interchanges](address-interchange.md).
The endpoint operator maps the stored form of the [logical array](logical-array.md) $g$ at the start of the route to its stored form at the end.
So the endpoint operator holds on every role of the [subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md).

established-multiplier.quote: Its cost bound contributes a term to the new algorithm's [cost table](cost-table.md).

exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Exact integer multiplication is measured by [running time cost](running-time-cost.md), counted on a machine whose alphabet and number of tapes are fixed in advance.

exceptional-set.quote: The exceptional set is a set of [Address](address.md) values, namely those at which the generic formula must be replaced by a special rule.

family-parameter.quote: A family parameter sets the sizes of the calls of the [Rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md).

fixed-tape-model.quote: This model decides the lower-bound question by the [limit inferior](limit-inferior.md) of the ratio $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)$.
This model measures its costs against [Schönhage–Strassen multiplication](schonhage-strassen.md).

This model states its lower bounds with [Big-Omega notation](big-omega-notation.md).

main-theorem.quote: The theorem gets its power saving from the [Rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md).

matrix-rank.quote: Matrix rank is defined using the vector spaces and linear maps of [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The rank of an edge matrix prices each edge change in the [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md).
The rank of $\mathcal{P}$ counts the rows that are [standard basis vectors](standard-basis-vector.md), which is the number of ones in $\mathcal{P}$.

middle-transform.quote: The middle transform is the inner step of [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which wraps it between two Gaussian maps.

mixed-radix-digits.quote: Uniqueness of the expansion is based on the [Telescoping identity](telescoping-identity.md).

modular-inverse.quote: A modular inverse is defined by a [congruence](congruence-modulo.md) modulo $p$: $h\mu$ and $1$ leave the same remainder on division by $p$, so $h\mu - 1$ is a multiple of $p$.

Conversely, the inverse is obtained from [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) applied to $h$ and $p$.
Each inverse supplies exponents for placing the [radix-digit coefficients](radix-digit-convolution.md) on cyclic axes.
Together the inverses help determine the generator of a [cyclic group](cyclic-group.md) of order $S$.

multidimensional-transform.quote: A multidimensional transform is a Fourier transform taken over several [transform axes](transform-axis.md) at once, computed by transforming along one axis at a time.
The multidimensional transform $\mathcal F$ is built from the [discrete Fourier transforms](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_{t_1},\dots,F_{t_D}$ by [tensor product](tensor-product.md).
Each axis transform is computed by the [radix-two factorization](radix-two-factorization.md) as $\lg t_\varsigma$ levels of butterflies, with multiplications by roots of unity between the levels.

multidimensional-transform.predicate: is written in the representation of
multidimensional-transform.quote: The multidimensional transform is written in the representation of [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md).
In this representation, the transform turns roots of unity into [signed cyclic shifts](cyclic-shift.md).

n-log-n-conjecture.quote: The conjecture bounds the cost of [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) from below.
The conjecture is negated through the [limit inferior](limit-inferior.md) of the ratio $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)$.

near-linear-time.quote: Near-linear time is built from the [Logarithm](logarithm.md) $\lg n$: it is the class of running times $O\big(n(\lg n)^{\Xi}\big)$, where $n$ is the input length.

negacyclic-convolution.quote: Negacyclic convolution is obtained from [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) by changing the sign of each term that wraps.

network-gate-terminal.quote: Each gate and terminal $v$ is a vertex type of [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md), and carries a frame $D_v$, an invertible linear operator on arrays.

neumann-series.quote: The Neumann series is defined over the linear operators of [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
Convergence is measured by the [array norm](array-norm.md), and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the operator norm induced by it.

normalization-scales.quote: Normalization scales undo the normalization of [Normalized cyclic convolution](normalized-cyclic-convolution.md).

normalized-cyclic-convolution.quote: A normalized cyclic convolution is a scaling of the [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) $f \ast g$ by the reciprocal of the sequence length.

normalized-cyclic-convolution.predicate: is turned into pointwise products by
normalized-cyclic-convolution.quote: A normalized cyclic convolution is turned into pointwise products by the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_s$ of length $s$, with $(F_s u)_k = \frac{1}{s}\sum_{j=0}^{s-1} u_j\,\omega^{jk}$.

A normalized cyclic convolution is computed by applying the [Transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), which keeps the source and target permutations in the formula so that they cancel across the convolution.
A normalized cyclic convolution is evaluated through [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which moves between coprime lengths and powers of two.
The transform $F_s$ takes its weights from powers of $\omega$, a primitive $s$-th [Root of unity](root-of-unity.md): a complex number with $\omega^s = 1$ whose smaller positive powers are not 1.

numerical-layer.quote: It computes the [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) on its selected bits, and its cost bound lets the [Rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md) save a power at each level.
The layer acts on the [record](payload.md) at each address, coefficient by coefficient.

opposite-transform.quote: The opposite transform $F_q^+$ is the sign-reversed form of the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md).

It maps products back from the [frequency domain](frequency-domain.md) to coefficients, which makes it the step that recovers convolution coefficients on the way to exact integer multiplication below $n\log n$.

opposite-transform.predicate: is applied to the result of
opposite-transform.quote: It is applied to the result of a [pointwise product](pointwise-product.md) of forward transforms.

opposite-transform.predicate: is applied along the axes of
opposite-transform.quote: The opposite transform is applied along the axes of an [array](array.md), one axis at a time.

order-of-element.quote: Within a [cyclic group](cyclic-group.md), the order of an element is read off from the group it generates.

orthogonal-complement.quote: The orthogonal complement $U^\perp$ of a subspace $U$ (a subset closed under addition and under multiplication by scalars) is defined by a [bilinear form](bilinear-form.md): it is the set of vectors that the form sends to zero against every vector of $U$.

packed-bit-addition.predicate: supplies the binary basis changes of
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition supplies the binary basis changes of the [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md).

packed-bit-addition.predicate: performs its basis changes in each
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition performs its basis changes in each [Transform round](transform-round.md).
Packed selected-bit addition adds selected bits by [Exclusive or](xor.md).
Packed selected-bit addition contributes one term to the [Cost table](cost-table.md) of the main theorem, which bounds exact multiplication of $n$-bit integers by $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.

It acts on two disjoint blocks, each an [Address field](address-field.md) of $L=fK$ address bits, a source $\mathcal{X}$ and a target $\mathcal{W}$, and it XORs one selected bit of each segment of $\mathcal{X}$ into the same bit of $\mathcal{W}$ at every address.
Packed selected-bit addition uses its third field as [Scratch storage](scratch-storage.md), $\mathcal{Z}$, whose initial value is arbitrary and must be restored.
Packed selected-bit addition exchanges its fields by the [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md).
Packed selected-bit addition has the form of an [Address shear](address-shear.md): each line adds a controlled $\pm1$ to one field according to a parity test on the other.

packed-bit-addition.predicate: updates its target field by a
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition updates its target field by a [Cyclic shift](cyclic-shift.md) controlled by the bits of the segments.

packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition bounds its exceptional set by a [Union bound](union-bound.md) over the $2(f-1)$ guards

packed-bit-addition.predicate: has its bound stated along a

padded-transform-box.quote: The padded transform box is the array of a [Multidimensional transform](multidimensional-transform.md) over its $D$ padded axes: the full array of entries that results once every axis has been padded to its chosen length.

The padded transform box is rearranged by the coordinate permutations of the [Transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), which move entries within this one fixed array instead of sorting the data into a new array.

The padded transform box is built from the [radix-digit coefficients](radix-digit-convolution.md) of the two integers, placed on pairwise coprime valid lengths $W_1,\dots,W_D$ by a [Chinese-remainder map](chinese-remainder-map.md) $\Phi$.
Expanding axis $s$ updates the box along each [line](axis-line.md) whose other coordinates are valid.

permutation.quote: A permutation of $\mathcal P$ is defined as a [bijection](bijection.md) of $\mathcal P$ onto itself, that is, a map $\upsilon$ from $\mathcal P$ to $\mathcal P$ that is one-to-one (no two positions have the same image) and onto (every position is an image).

phase-factor.quote: Each phase factor that is a power of $i$ is a unit of the [ring](ring.md) of Gaussian integers.
A phase factor used here is built from the fourth [roots of unity](root-of-unity.md), namely $1$, $i$, $-1$ and $-i$.

phase-factor.predicate: is applied at each sink of
phase-factor.quote: A scalar correction is a fixed constant phase factor applied at each sink of a [network of gates and terminals](network-gate-terminal.md).

phase-twist.predicate: is applied to the convolution from
phase-twist.quote: The twist is applied to the convolution from [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp-identity.md), which rewrites the [middle transform](middle-transform.md), the transform on the target lengths between the two Gaussian resampling maps, as a normalized cyclic convolution.

phase-twist.quote: The twist turns the last cyclic coordinate into a coefficient list of the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$](polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.md).
A phase twist acts on the last [cyclic coordinate](cyclic-coordinate.md), one axis of a multidimensional cyclic convolution, by multiplying each coefficient by a root of unity.

phase-twist.predicate: acts on the convolution form of
phase-twist.quote: The twist acts on the convolution form of the [middle transform](middle-transform.md), not on the transform itself.

pointwise-product.quote: The reason for multiplying transforms is the [convolution theorem](convolution.md): the pointwise product of transforms gives the transform of a convolution.

pointwise-product.predicate: is applied to the outputs of
pointwise-product.quote: On the way to fast integer multiplication, the pointwise product is applied to the outputs of two [forward transforms](forward-transform.md), and its result feeds the [Opposite transform](opposite-transform.md).

In the [Synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md), each entry is a polynomial rather than a number, and the product of two entries is taken in the [quotient ring](polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.md) $\mathbb{C}[y]/(y^r+1)$, where $y^r=-1$.

polynomial-ring.quote: The polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[y]/(\Xi)$ satisfies the axioms of a [Ring](ring.md).

polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: Convolution over the polynomial ring takes its products in the [Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1](polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.md)

Convolution over the polynomial ring computes its record products by [signed coefficient packing](signed-packing.md)
