Convolution over the polynomial ring extracts its blocks by a [carry scan](carry-propagation.md)
Convolution over the polynomial ring is computed along the [remaining axes](transform-axis.md)
holds each coefficient as [fixed-width digit blocks](fixed-width-digit-blocks.md)

polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.quote: This ring gives the arithmetic for [Synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md), whose roots of unity are powers of $y$.

prime-number.quote: A prime number is defined as an [Integer](integer.md) greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself.

prime-number.predicate: are used as axis lengths by
prime-number.quote: Distinct primes are used as axis lengths by a [Chinese-remainder map](chinese-remainder-map.md), which needs its axis lengths pairwise coprime.
Primes give axis lengths for the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md).
Each prime is the length of one [cyclic coordinate](cyclic-coordinate.md).

prime-source-lengths.quote: The distinct primes supply pairwise coprime lengths to the [Chinese-remainder map](chinese-remainder-map.md).
The lengths must give the separation that [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) needs
The lengths $s_1,\dots,s_d$ set the place values of the [Mixed-radix digits](mixed-radix-digits.md) of the $S$ positions
so the lengths satisfy the pairwise form of [Coprime](coprime.md).
The lengths are chosen as distinct [Prime number](prime-number.md)s.

projection-along-subspace.quote: A projection along a subspace is built from [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md) alone: it needs only vector spaces, subspaces and linear maps.

radix-digit-convolution.quote: Radix-digit convolution is a reduction of [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) to a convolution of short integer coefficients, obtained by writing each input as a polynomial in a power of two whose coefficients are its digits.
The convolution is computed with the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) at a power-of-two length $\mathcal{T}$ of at least $2\Upsilon-1$.

Radix-digit convolution computes its transforms from [Butterfly](butterfly.md) operations: each level applies a butterfly to each pair of positions whose indices differ in one bit, so a transform of length $\mathcal{T}$ has $\log_2 \mathcal{T}$ levels.
Radix-digit convolution states its bounds in [Big-Theta notation](big-theta-notation.md), so the costs below are $\Theta$ bounds.

radix-two-factorization.quote: The transform is built from [Butterfly](butterfly.md) maps arranged in $\lg q$ layers.
Radix-two factorization computes a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of length $q$, when $q$ is a power of two.

rank-saving-recursion.quote: The recursion runs on the wires of the [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md); each wire's fixed place is its role.
Rank-saving recursion reduces its calls to the [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md), one per unit of edge rank.
The same recursion applies to a [Numerical layer](numerical-layer.md), where the parameter counts selected axes instead of digits.
Rank-saving recursion gives each smaller call one [Stream](stream.md) of volume $V/W$.
Along a wire, the signed change telescopes across each [Incidence](incidence.md) to the sink dimension minus the source dimension.
The same signed-sum identity is checked on the [Complex construction](complex-construction.md), with ratio $101/539$.
Hence the smaller calls are counted for the [Bit construction](bit-construction.md) as $s=Wm-\mu+2\mathcal L$

The recursion is set in a fixed nondegenerate space $F$ of a [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md), a space with no nonzero vector orthogonal to all of $F$, of dimension $m$ (the letter $m$ changes meaning here).

recovery-and-error.quote: This step bounds the error of the [Convolution over the polynomial ring](polynomial-ring-convolution.md), which is computed by two forward synthetic transforms, a pointwise product and an opposite transform.
This analysis takes its guard widths from the [Guard-width bound](guard-width-bound.md), so every intermediate value is exact.
This analysis bounds the error of the [Phase twist](phase-twist.md) at each end by $4h_p$.
The analysis keeps every operand within the [Array norm](array-norm.md) bound of one.
This analysis handles each product as a [bilinear map](bilinear-map.md) $\mathcal{B}$ of approximate operands $f'$ and $g'$, which approximate $f$ and $g$.
The stage bound includes the error of the [Opposite transform](opposite-transform.md), which adds $E_s$ units.
The error analysis bounds the error over the $T$ entries of the [Padded transform box](padded-transform-box.md).
This analysis takes its scale from the [Prime source lengths](prime-source-lengths.md), whose product is $S$.
This uses the growth rule of [Little-o notation](little-o-notation.md) to conclude $\gamma=o(b)$, since $1/2+2\epsilon<1$.

The final scaling undoes the normalizations of the [Normalization scales](normalization-scales.md): $2^{2b+4}$ reverses the two digit scales ($\sigma^2=2^{-2b-4}$), and $S$ reverses the division by $S$.
Each scaling is exact on the integer [Grid numerator](grid-numerator.md) of each value, so it adds no error.
Thus the analysis keeps every entry in the [closed disk in the complex plane](complex-disk.md) of radius one.

ring.quote: A ring is a set with an addition and a multiplication that obey the usual rules of arithmetic, and the argument needs one because a ring gives the arithmetic of the [arrays](array.md) used here, whose entries are added and multiplied.
Residue rings are the arithmetic of the [fast multiplication of Schönhage and Strassen](schonhage-strassen.md).

ring-homomorphism.quote: Since $\Phi$ is an isomorphism, the [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of two sequences reduces to a product in the target ring
Bijectivity is verified through a [basis](linear-algebra-basics.md) of the target

schedule.quote: A schedule is built from [tape procedures](tape-procedure.md), applied one after another.

schonhage-strassen.quote: Schönhage–Strassen multiplication computes [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) of two $n$-bit integers in $O(n\log n\log\log n)$ time, and it is the bound that the paper's [main theorem](main-theorem.md) sharpens.
Schönhage–Strassen multiplication is based on [Congruence](congruence-modulo.md) modulo $2^\vartheta+1$: two integers are congruent when $2^\vartheta+1$ divides their difference.

schonhage-strassen.predicate: counts its roots of unity by
schonhage-strassen.quote: Schönhage–Strassen multiplication counts its roots of unity by the [Order of an element](order-of-element.md) of $2$, which is $8$ here.

schoolbook-multiplication.quote: Schoolbook multiplication is a method for [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md): it outputs the full $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit inputs, and it is exact for every input.

Schoolbook multiplication is the base case of a construction costed through its [logical bit volume](logical-bit-volume.md), which is needed because the construction's parameters are set only for large inputs.

scratch-storage.quote: The side and central wires of the [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) are scratch storage that is restored by that network, which lets it swap two data banks without changing its scratch values.

scratch-storage.predicate: restores values at every address of
scratch-storage.quote: Scratch storage restores values at every address of the [Address field](address-field.md) it occupies.

signed-packing.quote: Signed coefficient packing computes its integer products with the [Established O(n log n) multiplier](established-multiplier.md), used as an ordinary subroutine.
Signed coefficient packing is based on the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md): $f$ and $g$ are integer polynomials, and their product is taken there.
Signed coefficient packing recovers its coefficients from centered residues under [congruence modulo $B$](congruence-modulo.md).

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The layer expresses its phase frames through the [complex phase network](complex-phase-network.md), as products of $C$ on the selected bits.
The layer rests on [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md).
The layer moves its address chunks by [address-field interchange](address-interchange.md), a tape procedure.
The layer applies the length-two case of the [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) to each selected bit.
The layer is the tensor power of $H_0$ on the selected bits, written $H_0^{\otimes D}$, the [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of $D$ copies of $H_0$, one for each selected bit.

A simultaneous butterfly layer applies the two-point map of a [butterfly](butterfly.md) to one selected bit of each of several transform axes at once, computing the exact result in one tape procedure.
The layer acts on $D$ [transform axes](transform-axis.md), where $D$ is the number of axes.
The procedure ends with one final [truncation](truncation.md) of its values.

The layer groups the selected bits by [binary changes of basis](binary-change-of-basis.md), invertible row additions over the [binary field](binary-field.md) that relabel the bits, so that each group gives a smaller tensor product.
The layer is built from the [two-point kernel](two-point-kernel.md) $C$ on each selected bit.

stable-radix-sort.quote: The method is proved correct by [mathematical induction](mathematical-induction.md) on $t$, the pass index.

stable-radix-sort.predicate: makes each pass one scan of
stable-radix-sort.quote: Stable radix sort makes each pass one [scan](stream.md) of the extracted records and keys.
The method takes its pass count from the [base-2 logarithm](base-two-logarithm.md) of $M$, rounded up.
In the argument, stable radix sort sorts the records of the [exceptional set](exceptional-set.md), taken out of the full stream for separate sorting.

standard-basis-vector.quote: Each standard basis vector $\sigma_j$ is a basis vector of $F^m$ as defined in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).

stream.quote: Visiting data in streams is what lets a procedure run in [Near-linear time](near-linear-time.md), because a tape head cannot jump.
Each stream is scanned by a [Tape procedure](tape-procedure.md) in a fixed number of passes:
Each stream is formed by splitting an array on a specified digit of the [Mixed-radix digits](mixed-radix-digits.md) system.

stream.predicate: is carried by a wire of
stream.quote: Each stream is carried by a wire of a fixed [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md).

subset-intersection-network.quote: The network labels its wires with [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space $E$.

subset-intersection-network.predicate: is built within the framework of
subset-intersection-network.quote: The network is built within the framework of [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md), in which each wire is a role and each vertex carries a frame.
The labels' orthogonality and nondegeneracy are tested with the [bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) of $E$.
Nondegeneracy is checked through the [Eigenvalue](eigenvalue.md)s of the form matrix $I-J/9$.
Edge residuals are computed through the [Dual space](dual-space.md) $U'^{*}$, the linear functionals on $U'$.

subspace-labels.quote: Subspace labels are attached to each [Gate and terminal of a network](network-gate-terminal.md) of a linear network.
Labels take their orthogonality from its [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle$, and $\mathcal L$ denotes a label, a nondegenerate subspace of $E$.
Each vector $y$ of $\mathcal L'$ is paired with the [Linear functional](linear-functional.md) $\langle y,\cdot\rangle$ on $\mathcal L'$.
The frame $C_{\mathcal L}$ and its inverse have entries that are a [Gaussian integer](gaussian-integer.md) divided by $2^m$.

Labels compute their phase exponents with the [Projection along a subspace](projection-along-subspace.md) $\Theta_{\mathcal L}$ onto $\mathcal L$ along $\mathcal L^\perp$, which exists because $\mathcal L$ is nondegenerate.

Subspace labels are used in the [Bit network](bit-network.md), where they are carried by $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with form $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle=\xi^\top(I-J/9)\eta$, $\top$ transpose and $J$ the all-ones matrix.
The triple labels are drawn from a [Ground set](ground-set.md) $[h]$ of $h$ elements.
The triple labels are built from the [Indicator vector](indicator-vector.md) $t_T$ of each triple $T$.

The triple labels take the form of the [Line spanned by a vector](line-spanned-by-vector.md) $\operatorname{span}(t_T)$, and $\langle c\,t_T,t_T\rangle=2c\neq0$ for every nonzero $c$, so each triple line is nondegenerate.

supremum.quote: The set over which the supremum is taken is restricted by the [Array norm](array-norm.md) of $v$: only inputs with $\|v\| \le 1$ are used.

symmetric-matrix.quote: A symmetric matrix is a special case of the matrices in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).

synthetic-transforms.quote: Synthetic polynomial transforms are based on the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), with the root $\omega_N$ taken in $R_r$ in place of a complex number.

synthetic-transforms.predicate: start from the order given by
synthetic-transforms.quote: Synthetic polynomial transforms start from the order given by [Bit-reversed index order](bit-reversed-order.md): each record is first moved to its bit-reversed position, an address rearrangement with no arithmetic.

tape-procedure.quote: The first tape procedure, [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md), moves data between layouts by swapping two disjoint address fields of $u$ bits.
The second tape procedure does the butterfly part of each [transform round](transform-round.md) in one pass, applying the butterfly

tensor-product.quote: The tensor product is built from matrices, the basic objects of [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The tensor product takes its one-coordinate factor from the [Butterfly](butterfly.md) map $H_0$, which replaces a pair of values by its half-sum and half-difference.

transform-axis.quote: Along each axis the array is acted on by a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of length $\theta_\mu$.
On the remaining axes the transform weights its entries by powers of $y$, each a [Root of unity](root-of-unity.md).

transform-identity.quote: This identity computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which replaces a transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

Each permutation is defined by [congruence](congruence-modulo.md) of positions: $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo the length, where $u$ has length $s$ and $v$ has length $t$.
The identity depends on $s$ and $t$ being [coprime](coprime.md), so it pairs a transform of length $s$ with one of length $t$.
The identity is built from two [linear maps](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The identity cancels its permutations through the [opposite transform](opposite-transform.md) $F_s^+$, the transform with the exponent's sign reversed: $(F_s^+u)_k=\frac1s\sum_{j}u_je^{+2\pi ijk/s}$.
Each permutation reorders entries by a [bijection](bijection.md) of positions.
The proof builds its left inverse from a [diagonal scaling](diagonal-scaling.md) and $N^{-1}$ and a coordinate selection: a linear map $\Upsilon$ with $\Upsilon\Gamma=I$.
This identity avoids the [label-and-sort operations](stable-radix-sort.md), since $P_s$ and $P_t$ remain in the formula.
The invertibility of $N$ is proved with the [Neumann series](neumann-series.md): writing $N=I+E$ with $\|E\|<1$, the series $\sum_{k\ge 0}(-E)^k$ inverts $N$.

transform-layout.quote: The transform layout is built from [address-field interchange](address-interchange.md) moves of whole chunks, together with single-bit moves.
The transform layout prepares the input for each [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) of a transform round.

transform-layout.predicate: is applied within each round of
transform-layout.quote: The transform layout is applied within each round of the [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md).
The transform layout is consumed by the [opposite transform](opposite-transform.md).
The transform layout $\mathcal{L}$ is an explicit [permutation](permutation.md) of record addresses.
The transform layout keeps each element of the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md) that a record holds intact.

transform-layout.predicate: is the output order retained by
transform-layout.quote: The transform layout is the output order retained by the [forward procedure](forward-transform.md) for a pointwise product and the following opposite procedure.
The transform layout follows the pattern of the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), keeping its permutation in the computation.

transform-layout.predicate: places the selected bits of every
transform-layout.quote: The transform layout places the selected bits of every [participating axis](transform-axis.md) at one common offset, so one pass can apply a butterfly to all of them.
The transform layout counts its offsets from the [least significant end](address.md) of each address.

transform-round.quote: A transform round computes one stage of the [multidimensional transform](multidimensional-transform.md): every participating axis takes one butterfly step at once, then the twiddles are applied.
A transform round computes its butterfly by the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), which applies $\mathcal{B}$ in one pass.

truncation.predicate: is taken over pairs chosen by
truncation.quote: Truncation is taken over pairs chosen by their [addresses](address.md), with one rounding per layer.

two-point-kernel.predicate: is a matrix as defined in
two-point-kernel.quote: The two-point kernel $A$ is a matrix as defined in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md), here of size $2\times 2$:
The kernel $A$ has coefficients in [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md) when $p$ and $q$ are.
A two-point kernel is scaled by a [Phase factor](phase-factor.md), such as $i$, and its coefficients remain Gaussian dyadic.

union-bound.quote: The argument compares each outcome with the events that contain it and never compares events with one another, so the union bound does not require [Independence of events](independence.md) between the events.
Here the union bound is applied to events on the set of [addresses](address.md) in the rectangle, so $\Omega$ is that set.
Here the union bound bounds the exceptions to the [Guard-width bound](guard-width-bound.md), the addresses where a guard value leaves its good range.

xor.quote: XOR is a step inside the [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md), which swaps two disjoint fields of address bits.
So a sequence of XOR steps can produce a [Permutation](permutation.md) of the data, a rearrangement in which each value lands at exactly one position.
XOR is the only gate of the [Bit network](bit-network.md).

xor.predicate: is computed at each address by
xor.quote: XOR is computed at each address by a [Gate and terminal of a network](network-gate-terminal.md), which combines the two bits stored at that address by a fixed linear map.
